temperament: The signature prize sword everyone films — but the seasoned know the real jackpot is the sheath that won't let you bleed, and the whole floor is watching to see who lifts it.
game_hooks: ITEM-SEED (attuned legendary weapon + the real prize is the SCABBARD). Sword: a high-tier blade that only functions for a contestant who has proven 'rightful' worth (attunement/worth gate; PLACEHOLDER numbers — e.g. must hold a table-boss title or pass a worth-check). SCABBARD (the greater treasure, per Merlin's own line): while worn, the bearer takes NO bleeding — negates the bleeding condition entirely (PLACEHOLDER: bleeding immunity while equipped). Discoverable drawback: the scabbard can be STOLEN mid-run (Morgan's theft) — a rival patron lifts it and restores your bleeding vulnerability for the finale, then throws it in a lake, gone. Thrown back to the water at run's end (a return-the-relic hook tied to the Lady of the Lake and Bedivere).
rating_notes: Artifact, no worship = influence 1; recognition 5 (Excalibur is a household word). Item-seed. Normal table (object placement follows the table system).

epithets_traditional: the Cup of the Last Supper

temperament: The untouchable pot at the center of the room — feeds everyone, belongs to no one, and burns the hand of anyone who reaches for it unclean.
game_hooks: ITEM-SEED — the jackpot / ultimate-reward: endless nourishment + healing, achievable only by the 'sinless' (a zero-taboo-break / perfect-run gate). Achieving it ends the run at its peak (Galahad's rapture) for maximum payout; approaching it while flawed is ruinous (it harms the unworthy — the false seekers wither). PLACEHOLDER numbers. IP/SENSITIVITY: PD literary object BUT entangled with living Christian eucharistic symbolism — OWNER REVIEW REQUIRED before any irreverent casino framing (census sensitivity note; depiction_risk marked 'low' for that reason, not for cultic worship of the object itself).
rating_notes: Artifact, no liturgical worship of the object = influence 1; recognition 5 (household word). depiction_risk 'low' flags the LIVING CHRISTIAN eucharistic symbolism entanglement (census note) — owner review before irreverent framing; under depiction v2 this is data, not a hard gate, but the flag is retained deliberately. Item-seed / jackpot. Normal table.

temperament: The fellowship table with no head seat and one chair nobody dares — sit the oath and the whole party wins together; break it and the felt goes cold.
game_hooks: ITEM-SEED — fellowship/party-buff and a diegetic pun (it can LITERALLY be the VIP gaming table). 150 seats, no head (Malory: Uther's table, gifted via Leodegrance as Guinevere's dowry, made by Merlin). Equality buff: while seated, party members share a pooled bonus and no single member draws 'leader' target priority (flat threat). The Pentecost Oath is a run-modifier: accept its constraints (give mercy, flee treason, succour ladies/damosels) for a fellowship multiplier; break it and the table's boon collapses. Contains the lethal empty seat — see the Siege Perilous. PLACEHOLDER numbers.
rating_notes: Artifact, influence 1; recognition 4 ('knights of the round table' is broadly known; the object itself a notch below Excalibur/Grail). Item-seed / party-buff. Normal table.

symbols: letters of gold naming the destined

temperament: The one empty chair on the Forsaken floor with your name maybe on the rim — sit worthy and take the whole pot, sit unworthy and the house takes you.
game_hooks: ITEM-SEED — the lethal empty seat; a cursed-relic / Forsaken-table hazard and a perfect all-in staking piece. Any contestant who takes the seat UNWORTHY is destroyed (death_underworld — Malory: fatal to anyone unworthy); only the one destined contestant (Galahad-tier: a perfect / zero-breach record) may sit, and claims a top-tier reward + the Grail-quest unlock. Discoverable TELL: the seat's rim reveals the destined name in gold (a worth-check readout). A gamble object — sit if you dare, bet your existence on being the worthy one. PLACEHOLDER numbers.
rating_notes: Artifact, influence 1; recognition 2 (known to Arthurian-curious + comics audiences via the X-Men 'Siege Perilous', but not a household term). Cursed-relic / Forsaken-hazard item-seed — strong all-in staking object. Normal table.

temperament: The majority shareholder that never leaves the top-floor office: three religions' worth of brand equity consolidated into one bankroll, moving markets by memo while its staff work the floor.
game_hooks: NEVER an on-screen character (sacred-core protection). Present only as an off-screen investor institution: the influence-5 bankroll that funds VIP tables, buys out champions mid-run, and issues the boons that arrive through messenger staff (§3.3 safe-default 'boons via intermediaries'). Canon hook: the three Abrahamic brands are segmented fronts of THIS one holding company — a market-share play. World-event flavor: a hostile buy-out of a rival pantheon's champion, executed by suits, never by the boss in person.
rating_notes: Figure of living major religions (>100M) = influence 5 per rubric anchor; the God-concept is a global household name = recognition 5. Represented per canon as the abstract holding-company investor (sacred core never rendered as a character), so it draws no table crowd despite recognition 5 — an off-screen majority shareholder whose favor is mediated by staff.

temperament: The Firm's head of security in a charcoal suit, sidearm holstered, badge clipped — polite until you break a house rule, then he is the last thing your run sees.

favor_conditions: clear a room without logging a single forbidden/rule-breaking action
take a hit meant for a downed ally to keep them standing
defeat an encounter's lesser guards before its commander — break the chain of command from the bottom up
taboos: flee an encounter you started and leave an ally behind
sign a rival demon's contract mid-run while carrying his badge
patron_block.blessing_style: escalating defensive detail — fight by the book and the Firm's security assets show up on your side; boons arrive as backup and hardened guard, not flourish.

game_hooks: Patron-broker for the Firm's protection/war portfolio: you never deal with the boss, you deal with the account manager who carries a gun. Recurring NPC as VIP-table head of security who enforces house rules on-camera — corporate enforcer, suit not armor, never haloed.
rating_notes: Actively venerated across Christianity and named in Islam with feast days and shrine cults, but no independent >1M worship base of his own = influence 3 (saint/folk-cult tier); a games/comics and 'biblically accurate angel' staple = recognition 4 (cf. Amaterasu recognition 4).

temperament: Corporate communications with a golden lanyard — every announcement, every camera-call, every 'and now, live from the arena' runs through this one press office.

favor_conditions: trigger a camera-call / spectacle event and then win the encounter it framed
land a decisive blow on the first turn you enter a new district (make an entrance)
complete an objective exactly as it was publicly announced, no improvisation
taboos: silence or skip a broadcast/announcement event
win by anticlimax — grind a boss down with chip damage instead of a decisive finish
patron_block.blessing_style: hype economy — boons scale with audience attention; a well-delivered Gabriel bulletin multiplies your next spectacular action and your tips from the stands.

game_hooks: Patron-broker for the Firm's spectacle/media portfolio; the in-fiction bridge to the audience economy. NPC role: press office that stages your camera-calls and reads out objective terms. Corporate presentation only — lanyard and mic, never wings-as-icon.
rating_notes: Venerated herald across all three brands with active devotion but no independent mass cult = influence 3; the broadly known announcement-angel = recognition 4.

temperament: Chief of staff and keeper of the ledger, the account manager seated closest to the boss's door; nothing happens on the floor that his pen doesn't record.

favor_conditions: discover and read a boss's win-condition text before engaging it
finish a run with a complete, unbroken action record (no hidden/unlogged moves)
solve an encounter through a written or numeric puzzle rather than force
taboos: destroy or skip a lore/record object (leave a page in the archive unread)
break a promise you logged earlier in the same run
patron_block.blessing_style: front-loaded intelligence — boons are information: the ledger shows an enemy's schedule, a hidden exit, the exact turn a trap fires; never raw stats.

game_hooks: The wisdom/intelligence patron-broker and the diegetic explanation of the HUD/ledger — his 'records' are the game's information layer. NPC: chief of staff who audits your run. Enoch-becomes-Metatron backstory is story-only lore (Enoch the mortal is NOT an entity, per D-4).
rating_notes: Esoteric kabbalistic figure with devotion thin outside mysticism = influence 2; known to mythology/occult-curious audiences and a recurring games/anime name = recognition 3 (cf. Enki recognition 3).

epithets_traditional: Keeper of the Ledger of Names

temperament: The closer from accounts receivable, immaculately courteous, who arrives exactly when your ticket says he will and never one minute early or late.

favor_conditions: land a killing blow on an enemy at the precise moment it is marked/scheduled (execute on the appointed turn)
let a doomed-flagged enemy expire on its own timer instead of spending resources to finish it
carry a fallen ally's token to the end of the run rather than abandoning the body
taboos: cheat a death the ledger recorded (revive past the appointed count)
kill out of turn — slaughter a surrendered or already-doomed foe for spite
patron_block.blessing_style: the appointment — Azrael's boons are certainties, not chances: a guaranteed kill on a scheduled target, but never a second past the hour.

game_hooks: Dealer who settles final accounts at a table (tips buy timing, not force) and the death/timer patron-broker. Great as the impartial functionary the desperate try to bargain with. Name is folk-tradition (not in the Quran, which uses Malak al-Mawt) — safely depictable as staff.
rating_notes: Widely invoked angel of death in folk Islam and Western folklore with some active folk practice = influence 3; a recognizable name to game/comic audiences = recognition 3.

temperament: The floor's most famous degenerate — went all-in against the house once, lost everything, and has been working the comeback ever since, grinning like the pot is already his.

favor_conditions: decline the safe reward and take the higher-stakes option at a fork
win a Forsaken (VVIP) game solo after refusing all mid-run help
beat an enemy that outclasses you on paper (win while flagged the underdog)
taboos: accept a buy-out from the Firm or a messenger after signing with him
cash out early / win small instead of pushing the pot
patron_block.blessing_style: leverage — boons are loans against your future: enormous power now, a debt that compounds; he front-loads the comeback and lets you carry the risk.

game_hooks: The archetypal FORSAKEN HOST (the original all-in bet, existence staked and lost — §5). Boss sketch: NOT a damage race — Lucifer's arena is a rigged escalating wager; the discoverable win condition is to out-gamble him: refuse each doubling deal until his pride makes HIM over-commit, then the house collects the collateral (his own light). Condition affinities burn / dissolution as his radiance turns on itself. luck_gambling flag; forsaken_candidate flag.
rating_notes: No mainstream worship — theistic Satanism/Luciferianism is fringe (<1M) = influence 1; the Devil is a global household name = recognition 5. CALIBRATION: like Baba Yaga (inf 1/rec 4→normal) and the Zeus lesson (fame ≠ VVIP), recognition-5 fame with zero worship-wealth lands normal-tier — a spectacular Forsaken/boss figure, not a rich patron.

epithets_traditional: Lord of the Heavenly Dwelling (Ba'al Zebul)

temperament: Old money gone rancid: a demoted god who still throws around a fortune that smells of decay, buzzing with a retinue that eats what it touches.

favor_conditions: win an encounter by attrition — let poison or infection do the finishing work
turn an enemy's own numbers against it (make a swarm or summon kill its master)
hold a chokepoint for a set number of turns without yielding ground
taboos: cleanse or cure a condition you inflicted (waste the rot)
keep a clean, tidy killbox — refuse to let the field degrade
patron_block.blessing_style: spread — boons are contagions: buffs that multiply across a swarm and creep onto whatever you touch, strongest in a filthy, condition-soaked arena.

game_hooks: Boss sketch (swarm-attrition): Beelzebub is immune while his fly-cloud feeds on a filth-source; discoverable win condition is to locate and burn the corpse/refuse pile that spawns the swarm (fire), starving him — never out-DPS the cloud. Field conditions infected / poison / suffocation. Also a fine Forsaken host (a bankrupt ex-god). forsaken_candidate flag.
rating_notes: A demoted Philistine god (Ba'al of Ekron, 2 Kings 1) with no surviving worship = influence 1; 'Lord of the Flies' is broadly known across literature and games = recognition 4.

temperament: The contractor who built half the tables and remembers every load-bearing flaw — hands you the blueprints with a smile and dares you to lose while holding them.

favor_conditions: exploit an arena's structural flaw (use terrain or a hazard to win instead of raw force)
win an encounter without logging a single wrath-triggered action (stay cold)
complete a build/crafting objective to the exact spec
taboos: smash a mechanism you were meant to operate
let anger pick your target — attack whatever provoked you first
patron_block.blessing_style: engineering — boons are tools and blueprints; the demon who built the table hands you its schematics, so your power is using the room, not overpowering it.

game_hooks: Enemy/dealer with a rage-scaling gimmick: he grows stronger every time the player attacks in wrath, so the discoverable counter is to fight cold and use the arena he built against him (crushed via structural collapse; burn from the forge). Solomon-cycle material is IN via Asmodeus/Seal of Solomon/Shamir; Solomon the person stays OUT (D-4).
rating_notes: No mainstream worship = influence 1; a fixture of games and demon lore (D&D, Shin Megami Tensei) and the Tobit/Testament of Solomon cycles = recognition 4.

temperament: The one name on the floor no manager can put on an org chart — she walked out of the first arrangement ever offered and has been unbossable ever since.

favor_conditions: win a run entirely solo, refusing every companion or summon offered
escape a trap or cage encounter instead of fighting through it (fly, don't submit)
fight and win in a darkened / night-flagged arena
taboos: accept a subordinate role in a scripted hierarchy (willingly take orders from a table_boss NPC)
harm a child- or helpless-tagged NPC for reward
patron_block.blessing_style: sovereignty — boons make you ungovernable: escape, evasion, and night-power that grow the more you refuse to be controlled; nothing that binds you to another patron.

game_hooks: Boss sketch (ward-not-force): Lilith cannot be beaten down; the discoverable win condition is to recover and inscribe the protective ward of the three angels (Sanoy, Sansenoy, Samangelof, from the Alphabet of Ben Sira) to bind her, echoing the amulet legend. Field conditions chilled / bleeding. Modern feminist/Wiccan/Luciferian veneration is why she carries 'living'.
rating_notes: Small but organized modern veneration (Wiccan, feminist-spirituality, Luciferian) — the most-worshipped folk demon today = influence 2; a AAA-game headliner (Diablo IV) and broad cultural figure = recognition 4.

symbols: gilded scales tipped by a thumb
downcast gaze (always looking at the floor for gold)

temperament: The deepest pockets on the floor and the shallowest loyalty — backs whoever's up, folds on whoever's down, and calls it good business.

favor_conditions: end a run with the largest treasure haul on the board (top the greed leaderboard)
buy your way past an obstacle instead of fighting it (spend, don't sweat)
win a bidding war for a contested reward against a rival
taboos: give away loot for free (hand a reward to an ally without payment)
leave a treasure uncollected when you could have taken it
patron_block.blessing_style: liquidity — boons are purchasable and instant, the deepest pockets on the floor; but he backs only whoever's winning and drops a losing book without sentiment (buy-out magnet — lowest fidelity on the roster).

game_hooks: The casino's native demon — 'the only fiend every casino already worships without knowing.' Dealer/patron who models the fidelity=1 buy-out mechanic (sells your contract the instant your odds dip). Enemy variant: a greed-trap boss immune while treasure remains on the field; win condition is to leave the hoard untouched (every coin taken empowers him; crushed via burial in gold, exhausted).
rating_notes: No worship (a personification of greed, Matthew 6:24; personified by Milton and Spenser) = influence 1; broadly recognized 'god of money' = recognition 3.

epithets_traditional: the Sea-Monster God Made to Play With
the Banquet at the End of Days
King over the Children of Pride

temperament: Not a gambler — the table itself when the game is the sea; the house wheels it out when a champion needs to be reminded how small they are.
game_hooks: Colossal boss / arena-beast (size class: leviathan). NOT a damage race — Job 41 frames it as unkillable by force ('canst thou draw out leviathan with a hook?'), so the discoverable win condition is environmental: recover the great Hook, drain/plug the flooding arena, or bait it into its counterpart Behemoth so the two slay each other (the end-of-days banquet myth, Bava Batra 74b). Field conditions suffocation (the flood) / chilled (the deep) / crushed (the coils).
rating_notes: A monster, never worshipped = influence 1; a household sea-monster name across games and film = recognition 4 (rubric anchors 'dragons' near the top of recognition).

temperament: The saint the desperate pray to when every other patron has passed — generous to the outlaw and the orphan alike, and merciless to anyone who breaks a promise to her.

favor_conditions: take a champion flagged doomed / lowest-odds into a Forsaken game and survive
keep a vow made to her for the entire run (honor a self-imposed rule to the letter)
finish the strong and the weak enemies alike, sparing none for reward (show death no favoritism)
taboos: break a promise sworn to her on camera
court a rival patron while carrying her favor (she is the jealous saint)
patron_block.blessing_style: the impartial hand — boons come to anyone who asks sincerely, outlaw or saint; generous and unconditional up front, then withdrawn with terrifying speed the instant a vow is broken.

game_hooks: Highest-influence folk patron and a natural FORSAKEN HOST — the saint of the nothing-to-lose, perfect for the doomed-champion frame (§5). Devotional lore drives her extreme personality (generosity 5 to the faithful, wrath 5 / jealousy on a broken vow — Chesnut). luck_gambling flag (petitioned for fortune). Carries 'living' (10â€“12M devotees, Church-condemned) â€” doubly sensitive; depict respectfully.
rating_notes: 10â€“12M living devotees (Chesnut, verified via Patheos/academia) = influence 4, matching the Amaterasu anchor; broadly recognized via news, tattoos, and TV = recognition 4.

temperament: A folk saint on a barstool, cigar lit and glass full, who will fix your luck and greenlight your revenge for the price of an offering the other patrons would call vulgar.

favor_conditions: spend or offer a consumable ('vice' item) before an encounter and then win it
win by trickery or an ambush rather than a fair fight
take revenge on an enemy that previously defeated you (rematch and win)
taboos: arrive empty-handed — court his favor without an offering in the log
moralize — refuse a dirty-but-effective tactic he offered
patron_block.blessing_style: the crooked favor — plied with offerings he tilts luck your way and greenlights tactics other patrons forbid; cheap to court, but the help is always a little crooked.

game_hooks: Low-recognition, rare-board patron with high collector appeal (obscurity 'rare'): the offering-driven luck patron who explicitly grants revenge and success-at-others'-expense (verified petition profile). luck_gambling flag. Carries 'living' AND 'restricted' â€” only widely-published public-sphere material used; the cofradÃ­a's ritual specifics (Santiago AtitlÃ¡n) are community-held and NOT collected. Owner-gate advised.
rating_notes: Active Tz'utujil cofradÃ­a practice, regional in scale = influence 3 (folk-saint cult tier); little recognition outside Guatemala/travel media = recognition 2 â†’ rare board, collector appeal.

epithets_traditional: the Being Whose Off-Switch is an Edit

symbols: Hebrew word emet (××ž×ª) on the forehead

temperament: House muscle with an off-switch you can read: a clay guardian that runs on a written word, unstoppable until someone edits it.
game_hooks: ITEM/CONSTRUCT SEED: a summonable clay guardian-ally whose 'durability' is a written Name (emet / ××ž×ª on the brow, or a shem-slip in the mouth). Signature mechanic straight from the legend â€” its off-switch is an EDIT: erase the aleph and emet ('truth') becomes met ('dead') and it collapses to inert clay. Failure state: if the Name is defaced by an enemy mid-fight it goes berserk and turns on its summoner (crushed damage; no bleeding/poison â€” it is unfeeling clay). Rabbi Loew the maker is story-only lore, NOT an entity (D-4 real human).
rating_notes: An artifact/construct, no worship = influence 1; a household concept across games, film, and modern AI discourse = recognition 4 (cf. Baba Yaga folk-class, normal tier despite high recognition).

epithets_traditional: he for whom the table is set

temperament: The oldest patron in the room and the most literal â€” the god you set a table for before the word 'casino' existed, who deals in nothing but the tilt of the odds.

favor_conditions: win an encounter decided by a coin-flip / low-odds outcome (let the gamble land)
set an offering at a shrine or table before a run and then complete the run
take the riskier of two offered paths and clear it
taboos: hedge every bet â€” never take an offered high-risk/high-reward option across a whole run
curse your luck aloud after a bad outcome (blaspheme against fortune)
patron_block.blessing_style: pure fortune â€” boons are reweighted dice: Gad doesn't make you stronger, he makes the improbable break your way; the casino's oldest and most literal patron.

game_hooks: The purest luck_gambling patron in the corpus â€” casino nobility despite the honest-floor scores. Mythic obscurity = rare on the boards, a collector's thrill when Fortune himself bids (canon rule). Flavor is literal: Isaiah 65:11 condemns apostates who 'set a table for Gad (Fortune) and fill mixed wine for Meni (Destiny)' â€” i.e. the first gambling shrine, condemned by the very Firm he now works alongside. Pair with Meni (Destiny) for a two-croupier event. luck_gambling flag.
rating_notes: Extinct pan-Semitic luck cult, remembered by specialists = influence 1, recognition 1 (the honest floor, cf. Zababa) â€” mythic obscurity means rare boards and collector appeal, not padding.

epithets_traditional: Ra-Horakhty (Ra, Horus of the Two Horizons)

symbols: solar disk encircled by a uraeus (cobra)
the solar barque (Mandjet by day, Mesektet by night)
animals: ram (the night-sun descending into the Duat)

temperament: The reigning house king and old money in the most literal sense — he lit the first table and has sailed the same day-and-night circuit ever since, personally beating back the thing in the dark; imperious, punctual, and quietly terrified of the shift when the staff decide he's grown too old to run the floor.

favor_conditions: Advance sun-like: clear a floor without ever re-entering a room you have already cleared (forward course only — the barque never sails back).
Land the killing blow yourself on a chaos-, serpent-, or darkness-class enemy, or deliver a boss's killing blow during a lit / daylight phase of the encounter.
Clear every objective on a floor in one unbroken push and extract before taking any rest.
Set up a kill and let your summoned enforcer, pet, or a marked teammate deliver the finishing blow (rule through your Eye, as Ra acts through Sekhmet/Hathor).
taboos: Retreat backward through a room you have already cleared — the sun does not reverse its course.
Let a full darkness / 'night' phase pass without defeating what ambushes you in it (you left Apep unanswered).
Mock, insult, or plot against a patron, host, or elder on camera — the offense that once made him loose the Eye on all mankind.
patron_block.blessing_style: Radiant but delegated — his favor arrives through an intermediary 'Eye' (a summoned enforcer or a marked ally) rather than his own hand; bright, order-restoring buffs that peak in lit phases, gutter in darkness, and must be re-earned at each new 'dawn'.

game_hooks: The reigning house king and faction head above his own Eye (Sekhmet) — the establishment patron whose backing signals old-money legitimacy at any table. Boon delivery is diegetically routed through an 'Eye' intermediary (summon / marked-ally), matching the myth in which Ra strikes through Sekhmet/Hathor/Bastet rather than directly. Time-of-day motif for events: Khepri (dawn scarab) → Ra (midday falcon) → Atum-Ra (dusk) → ram-headed night-sun descending into the Duat — a recurring day/night phase cycle. Recurring 'night phase' hazard: Apep besieges the light every night (already an extracted boss, myth_egyptian_nightly_execration_of_apep) — Ra's tables run a defend-the-barque-until-dawn beat. Wrath / lore trigger: the Destruction of Mankind (he loosed the Eye as Sekhmet for humanity's mockery, then relented with the red-beer flood) seeds his on-camera-insult taboo and a 'called off at the brink' mercy mechanic. Optional decline arc for a later Forsaken-adjacent lens: the aged Ra whose bones turned to gold and hair to lapis, who withdrew to the sky on Nut's back and delegated rule to Osiris/Horus.
rating_notes: Influence 2 — Egyptian-core / Zeus anchor (extinct organized cult, deep cultural continuity, only a low-thousands Kemetic revival), same tier as every other core netjer in this tradition; recognition 5 — global household-name sun-god (Stargate, Smite, Age of Mythology), on par with calibration Anubis (2/5). VIP not VVIP per §3.5: at influence 2, fame alone does not buy the top table.

epithets_traditional: Eledumare (the All-Sufficient; the source of creation that never empties)
Olofin Orun (Owner of the Law of Heaven)

symbols: the open sky (Olorun = Owner of the Sky)
the source of ashe (vital force in all things)

temperament: The unseen proprietor above every table: the source of the ashe the whole floor gambles with, who assigned each soul its odds before it was born and has never once come down to play. Serene, impartial, and utterly remote.
game_hooks: STORY-ONLY / off-board source. Olodumare is the divinity economy's ultimate bankroll and origin point -- the source of all ashe (the divine currency the orishas wager) -- but he keeps no shrine of his own and receives no direct offerings: adherents reach him only through the orishas. That theology makes him a poor playable patron and a perfect off-screen presence: the owner of the whole building nobody sees on the floor, whose word settles cosmology (he alone judged the seventeenth-orisha and cloth-contest disputes) and whose court is where destiny is chosen and exile is decreed. Every orisha's boon is, in the last analysis, borrowed ashe of his. Use him as lore glue and an abstract investor tier; never render him as an interactable NPC. Closes the dangling myth-participant edges (he appears in five extracted myths as the High God) and the reciprocal relation edges from Babalu-Aye (exiled from his court), Olokun (challenged him), and Oduduwa (commissioned by him to create land).
rating_notes: Apex of the LIVING Yoruba orisha tradition = influence 4 (rubric band 4 names 'Yoruba orishas'; Amaterasu-consistent, below Ganesha 5) -- influence measures the worship-weight of the tradition behind him, which is the whole family's, so his remoteness/no-direct-cult drives the story_only disposition, not the score. Recognition 2 (encyclopedia/mythology-curious depth; the remote High God is far less pop-famous than Shango or Anansi -- matches the batch's Orunmila/Olokun 2; sits at the 2/3 edge).

epithets_traditional: Olofin Otete (who took the Basket of Existence from Olodumare)

symbols: sixteen-branched palm tree (the sixteen founding kingdoms)
the chain let down from heaven

temperament: The founding king who seized the table when its rightful dealer passed out drunk -- built a dynasty on one decisive move while his brother slept off the palm wine, and every crown on the floor now traces its licence back to him. Exacting about ground held and oaths kept.

favor_conditions: reach and claim the floor's central objective or founding anchor before any rival contestant or the clock can seize it
capture a room or checkpoint and hold it -- finish the floor without ever ceding control of the ground you claimed
win a run in which you take command after your leader or an ally falls, and carry the party's objective to the exit yourself
convert a rival's fumbled or abandoned objective into your own win -- found your victory on their lapse
taboos: abandon or surrender a foothold, room, or objective you claimed and swore to hold
break an oath of leadership or a pact of sovereignty sworn on camera
let a rival take the founding prize through your own idleness or intoxication (the very failure that gave you your throne)
patron_block.blessing_style: the founder's charter -- boons reward being first and holding ground: claim-and-hold bonuses on captured objectives, territory-control auras that strengthen the longer you keep a room, and one per-run 'coronation' that turns a held objective into a lasting run-long advantage

game_hooks: Patron of founder / leader / claim-first / hold-the-ground builds. His creation myth IS the mechanic: sent to make dry land, Obatala drank palm wine and slept, so Oduduwa took the snail-shell of sand, the five-toed hen, and the palm nut, descended at Ile-Ife, and scratched the world's first land into being -- literally the seize-the-contested-objective play already written into myth_yoruba_west_african_obatala_oduduwa_creation. Sponsors 'first to the objective' and territory-control run formats. Lore: the sixteen-branched palm = the sixteen kingdoms his descendants founded, a ready-made 16-node origin map; Ile-Ife is the 'origin table' whose licence every other table inherits. EUHEMERISM NOTE (owner awareness): tradition also names him a historical first king (~800-1000 CE, a migrant prince who subdued Ife's aborigines); venerated today as a founding orisha, so included as a god per the Shango precedent -- the legend cycle is the entity, not the historical person (respects D-4). Closes Obatala's dangling supplanted_by edge and adds the reciprocal to Olodumare's commission.
rating_notes: Venerated founding orisha of the LIVING Yoruba tradition, central to Yoruba identity and kingship (Ile-Ife the sacred origin city) = influence 4, consistent with the orisha band and Amaterasu 4 (3 is defensible since his veneration is more dynastic/ancestral than a broad sacrificial cult -- flagged, within ±1). Recognition 2: the name Oodua/Oduduwa is widely known in Nigeria and in encyclopedias but carries little global pop-culture draw -- Orunmila/Olokun tier.

symbols: the sun and the open sky

temperament: The sky-high proprietor who owned every story before the spider bought them. Names an impossible price with a perfectly straight face -- and pays out to the letter the instant you actually meet it. The house that keeps its word.

favor_conditions: declare a stake or handicap before a run and honor it in full to the end, whatever it ends up costing you
complete a full multi-target bounty -- subdue or retrieve every named objective on the board without leaving a single one behind (the four-captures template)
win a run without breaking one promise, contract, or bargain you made on camera
taboos: renege on a declared wager or a price you agreed to pay
claim a reward whose full price you did not actually pay
patron_block.blessing_style: the sky-god's contract -- favor arrives from overhead (rain cover, high-ground vision, aerial reconnaissance of the floor) plus one per-run 'name your price' bargain: pledge a real stake and receive a matched boon, paid out to the letter exactly if you meet the terms

game_hooks: Patron of contract / wager / impossible-fetch builds, and the casino's deepest lore glue for the story economy: Nyame is who Anansi BOUGHT the world's story-catalog from (for the price of Onini the python, the Mmoboro hornets, Osebo the leopard, and the Mmoatia fairy). So every rerun-royalty and epithet-ceremony payout that flows to Anansi traces back to Nyame's original sale -- he is the prior owner of the broadcast rights. Sets 'name your price' run contracts and honors any bet paid in full; his story-wager myth is the zero-kill capture-gauntlet template shared with Anansi. DISTINCT high god from Olodumare (Akan, Ghana -- not Yoruba); both remote sky-supremes of the West African family, filed under the same census bucket per Anansi's pantheon 'akan' -- do NOT merge them in Wave-4 dedup. Unlike Olodumare he is patron_capable: myth gives him direct agency as a bargaining counterparty. Closes Anansi's dangling wagered_against edge (reciprocal, symmetric).
rating_notes: Supreme creator sky-god of the LIVING Akan tradition, directly invoked via the Nyame dua altar and Gye Nyame (more directly venerated than the ultra-remote Olodumare) = influence 4, consistent with the orisha band and Amaterasu 4 (3 defensible -- Akan supreme-being veneration is diffuse and aniconic, no sacrificial priesthood; flagged, within ±1). Recognition 2: encyclopedia/mythology-curious depth, with faint reflected recognition as 'the sky-god Anansi bought the stories from,' far below Anansi's own 4.

symbols: the sealing boulder of Yomotsu Hirasaka

temperament: Founding chairman of the eight-million-talent agency: he built the whole company with his wife, walked out of the basement alive when she died down there, washed the grave off himself, and split the empire between his three star children — now semi-retired upstairs on Awaji, still signing the checks and warding the door he sealed behind him.

favor_conditions: Cleanse yourself of every condition at a spring or purification tile after clearing a death-zone floor, then win the next fight while clean (his misogi rite)
Answer a party death by fathering the comeback: revive or field a replacement for a downed/killed ally and still win the floor (his 1,500-births-a-day counter to death)
Descend into a death-zone to recover a lost ally or item, then get back out alive and seal the route behind you
Found something that lasts mid-run — capture and hold a room, node, or objective others abandoned
taboos: End a floor still carrying rot — poison/infected/dissolution left uncleansed (he cannot abide the pollution of death)
Chase a lost cause into a wipe instead of sealing the loss and rebuilding (his hard lesson at Yomotsu Hirasaka: wall it off, make new life)
Break the order of the rite — act or speak out of the declared sequence (Hiruko was born malformed because the bride spoke first)
patron_block.blessing_style: The founder's clean slate: his favor arrives as purification and renewal — he strips conditions, reseeds a downed roster, and blesses new ground you claim; boons that let you walk out of a death-zone unspoiled and rebuilt rather than power that keeps you grinding inside it.

game_hooks: PATRON — the life-side counterpart to Izanami's collections desk; the two are a matched primordial pair sealed apart at Yomotsu Hirasaka, so courting one risks the other's rival-curse (his purification boons directly undo her rot). Signature event: a MISOGI cleansing station — step off a defiled death-zone floor into his spring to strip every stacked condition and pick one persisting elemental boon (light / night / storm, echoing the three-children division). Founder's-comeback economy: where Izanami calls in a daily kill quota, Izanagi answers with a birth/revive quota — he pays out when you turn a near-wipe into a fielded comeback (1,500 to her 1,000). Retired-chairman flavor: an off-screen elder INVESTOR who bankrolls from Awaji, showing up in person only when a run reaches the founding myths. His creation act (churning Onogoro from the brine with Ame-no-nuboko) seeds a 'claim and hold new ground' favor.
rating_notes: Primordial creator god with a real but localized major cult — Izanagi Jingū on Awaji (venerated as Japan's oldest shrine, his palace-and-tomb seat) and Taga Taisha in Shiga both enshrine him as principal kami (verified) = influence 3, matching his consort Izanami and short of the recognition-driven 4s (Amaterasu/Susanoo/Inari/Okuninushi) that head the tradition ceiling. Recognition 3 via Persona/SMT-class game fame and the mythology-curious tier — below the torii-and-sun visual shorthand of the recognition-4 kami; consistent with Izanami 3/3, Tsukuyomi 3/3, and the Väinämöinen recognition-3 anchor.

symbols: the sword Hrotti in the hoard
a concealed trench beneath the wyrm's path

temperament: The high-roller who cashed out of life itself — traded his body, murdered his own father and cheated his brother for the pot, then coiled on it forever; the casino's cautionary shape of a winner who won so hard he became the safe and will never reopen it.
game_hooks: Enemy sketch — size class: huge-to-colossal wyrm, a hoard-guardian that never leaves its gold. Condition affinities: poison and infected (the venom it breathes into the earth — a spreading contamination field around the lair), exhausted (attrition from crossing the poison perimeter plus the terror it radiates), bleeding (only from the one soft place), crushed (coil and tail slams). Discoverable win condition — NOT a damage race: the dorsal scales are impervious (topside strikes chip and rebound to zero) and the Ægishjálmr 'Helm of Awe' projects a fear aura forcing disadvantage that drives attackers off while they stand in its gaze. The discovery: the wyrm crawls a FIXED path from its bed to water; dig or hide in a concealed trench beneath that path so the unarmored underbelly passes overhead for a single decisive thrust (Sigurd's tactic — the belly takes bleeding and the beast bleeds out). Greed trap layered on the kill: the hoard is cursed (Andvaranaut) — looting the gold stamps a transferable curse affix on the taker (ties directly to Sigurd's cautionary arc and game_hooks), so the real test is whether a contestant can win the vault and survive owning it. Optional dying-words phase: a briefly conversant, fate-taunting boss who names the curse before he goes.
rating_notes: Beast, no cult = influence 1 (Fenrir/Jörmungandr tier). Named dragon carried by Wagner's Ring (Fafner), the Völsung/Nibelung redactions, God of War and pervasive game/anime use = recognition 4 — one below the generic 'dragons'=5 rubric line, level with slayer Sigurd (also 4) and the Baba Yaga folk-monster anchor (4), inside the ±1 band. PD literary (Fáfnismál + Völsunga saga); ships freely — Marvel/Capcom 'Fafnir' uses exist but only the myth figure is PD.

symbols: the arm and claw torn at the shoulder, nailed beneath Heorot's gable
barred mead-hall doors that will not keep him out
the blood-trail down into the fen-mere

temperament: The uninvited regular who cannot stand the house's music — crashes the party every night to eat the winners in their sleep, and keeps getting away with it right up until the one contestant who refuses to draw a weapon meets him grip for grip.
game_hooks: Enemy sketch — size class: large humanoid ogre (accursed kin of Cain), a night-raider who strikes only after dark. Condition affinities: crushed (the bare-handed clinch and the joint-break), bleeding (the shoulder-wound once the limb is torn free), suffocation (the grapple-lock and the collapsing hall), exhausted (stacked on anyone who wastes stamina swinging steel). Discoverable win condition — NOT a damage race: Grendel is charm-warded against edged weapons — every sword, axe, or spear strike deals ZERO and no blade will bite him (the poem's own rule), so a weapon loadout can NEVER lower his health. The discovery, matching his own handicap: disarm completely and win the unarmed GRAPPLE — lock his arm, pile crushed on the limb until the joint gives, and tear it from the socket at the shoulder; matching his no-weapons handicap banks the fair-fight hype (audience multiplier, the 'Grendel's-Bane' epithet already seeded on the Beowulf entity). Night-phase framing: he bars and bursts the hall doors, running an environmental collapse/suffocation hazard alongside the clinch. Second-phase seed: mortally maimed, he flees to the fen-mere — an optional avenger encounter (his mother, not yet extracted) waits underwater for a follow-up run.
rating_notes: Monster, no cult = influence 1 (Fenrir/Jörmungandr tier). Global curriculum staple plus film and novel adaptations (Zemeckis 2007, John Gardner's 'Grendel') = recognition 4 — level with slayer Beowulf (4) and the Baba Yaga folk-monster anchor (4), inside the ±1 band; below the household-name 5s. variants: the Signet of the Most Great Name

temperament: An instrument of absolute authority with no will of its own: press it to a demon's chest and the proudest fallen power becomes house labor — but it obeys whoever holds it, and the last one to hold it owns everything the last one bound.
game_hooks: ITEM/RELIC SEED (numbers PLACEHOLDER, R14). A rare wearable signet the contestant equips; NOT a damage item but a CONTROL relic straight from the Testament of Solomon (Conybeare 1898) and Talmud Gittin 68a-b. Signature mechanic: pressing the Seal on a subdued demon-tier boss COMPELS it into temporary bound service instead of killing it — the 'set to labor' turn (haul, demolish a wall, turn on its own lieutenants) that the Asmodeus/Beelzebub myths reenact. Two-mode from Gittin 68b (ring 'partly brass and partly iron'): the brass face commands cooperative bound spirits, the iron face compels the hostile ones. LOSS/FAILURE STATE from Gittin 68: a bound demon can trick the holder into surrendering the ring and swallow it or cast it into the sea — lose the Seal and every demon you bound turns on you at once (the 'false Solomon' usurpation); you must recover it from a fish/loot-cache to restore control. Diegetically staged as the house's binding-signet — how demon-princes (Asmodeus 'the contractor who built the tables', Beelzebub) got bound to the Cosmic Casino in the first place. CASINO-ROLE NOTE: the enum has no 'relic/loot' value; tagged 'dealer' as least-wrong (a house-side implement of contract-enforcement), NOT 'story_only' (which the spec reserves for non-gameplay lore, and an artifact is an explicit gameplay class).
rating_notes: An object/relic, never an object of worship = influence 1; 'Solomon's ring that commands demons' and the hexagram Seal are ubiquitous across games, occult, and pop culture = recognition 4 (cf. golem 4, Leviathan 4). Influence 1 -> normal tier per §3.5.

temperament: The Firm's in-house prosecutor who is himself a devil: the venom in every contract, the accuser at your shoulder reading back your own violations, married to the one name the org chart can't erase — and betting on your fall the whole time.

favor_conditions: win an encounter with poison / venom / a damage-over-time affliction as the killing method rather than a direct blow (let the venom do the work)
expose a hidden breach — bring a documented cheat or rule-break by an enemy or rival to a table_boss / house arbiter and win the ruling against them
bait a marked target into breaking its own oath or triggering its own condition so it falls by its own hand, not yours
deliver the finishing hit only to a foe already afflicted or dying (execute the condemned, never the healthy)

shield or excuse a rule-breaker you could have accused
swear falsely on any contract that carries his mark
patron_block.blessing_style: corrosion and accusation — boons are slow poison and legal leverage: your strikes fester and stack over time, and the house's own rules bend to the charges you file against a marked target; attrition and paperwork, never a clean decisive blow.

game_hooks: Patron NPC: the Firm's accuser/internal-affairs on the payroll who is ALSO a prince of demons (the 'messenger-on-the-payroll-who-is-also-a-demon' flagged in the dossier cross-links) — you don't fight him, you sign with him, and his boons are venom stacks and the leverage to prosecute a rival's cheat at the table. Angel-of-death framing: he marks a target and lets the appointed poison/doom run its course (contrast Azrael the impartial closer — Samael is the venomous, partisan one). Consort of Lilith (the unbossable one): courting Samael while carrying her favor, or vice-versa, is a rival-curse flashpoint (pettiness-driven). Forsaken-host candidate — the accuser wagers on souls (the Job frame). symbols: a pasture of a thousand mountains

temperament: Not a gambler and barely a fighter — the immovable land itself given hunger: it grazes a thousand mountains flat and lies in the reeds, placid until the appointed end-day when it and the sea rise to destroy each other for the crowd's feast.
game_hooks: Colossal land/desert arena-beast (size class: leviathan-class), the earth mirror of abrahamic_folk_leviathan. NOT a damage race — Job 40:19 frames it as unkillable by force ('he that made him can make his sword to approach unto him' — only its Maker can). DISCOVERABLE WIN CONDITIONS, all sourced: (1) the end-of-days myth (Bava Batra 74b; 1 Enoch 60:7-9) has Behemoth and Leviathan SLAY EACH OTHER — bait Behemoth into its sea-counterpart Leviathan so the two destroy one another (the exact mirror of Leviathan's own 'bait it into Behemoth' hook, so the pair share one arena solution); (2) its whole strength is EATING — it 'grazes on a thousand mountains' and 'drinketh up the Jordan' (Job 40:23), so burn/deny its grazing or drain/divert its river to starve the titan until it collapses EXHAUSTED; (3) its power is bulk — trample and collapse deal CRUSHED, and burying the earth-titan in its own landslide deals SUFFOCATION. Field conditions (rulebook only): crushed (trample/bulk), exhausted (starve the grazer), suffocation (bury the land-beast). Pairs with Leviathan for a VVIP end-of-days double-boss where the win is to make the two kill each other.
rating_notes: A monster, never worshipped = influence 1 (matching its sea-counterpart Leviathan); 'behemoth' is both a common English word for the colossal and a recurring game monster (Final Fantasy, D&D, Monster Hunter) = recognition 4, tied to Leviathan (4). Influence 1 -> normal tier.

temperament: Gad's silent partner and opposite number: where Fortune reweights the dice, Destiny only reads the number already written — the croupier who never reshuffles because the outcome was settled before you sat down.
game_hooks: The destiny-croupier of Gad's two-god table (Isaiah 65:11: apostates 'prepare a table for Gad [Fortune], and furnish the drink offering unto Meni [Destiny]'). MINOR DEALER, not a patron — a one-verse deity, kept honest to its thin attestation. Mechanical contrast to abrahamic_folk_gad: Gad reweights the dice toward the improbable (random luck); Meni ENFORCES the fixed/appointed outcome — his table resolves to the pre-written result with no reroll, an anti-luck 'the number is already set' mechanic. Runs the two-croupier event with Gad (Fortune deals the gamble, Destiny collects the sentence). Manah root = 'to count / apportion / assign'. WAVE-4 SYNCRETIC LEAD (handle with care): Meni is academically linked to the pre-Islamic Arabian goddess Manat (fate/doom, one of the three 'daughters'); Manat is NOT extracted and is Islamic-sacred-adjacent, so treat as a note only, not an assertion. luck_gambling flag (casino nobility per §4).

Zababa 1/1, Gad 1/1), so mythic obscurity: rare on the boards, a collector's thrill when Destiny itself deals.

Aeschylus, Eumenides 723-728 (Perseus, Smyth note) — Apollo plies the Moirai with wine to win Admetus a reprieve
Apollodorus 1.4.2 + Ovid, Metamorphoses 6.382-400 — the Marsyas music contest and flaying (the hubris/taboo demonstration)
Theoi Project (theoi.com/Olympios/Apollon.html) — sourced compendium: Hekatebolos/far-shooter, Phoebus, and the later solar identification with Helios

temperament: The casino's deposed old chairman — once the whole floor was his, now he holds one soma-soaked table and keeps re-mortgaging the throne to prove he still rules the family.

favor_conditions: open every boss room with your single strongest declared strike, before the enemy acts (the vajra falls first)
defeat a gate-keeper that dams or hoards a resource the party needs — water, loot, or passage — and release it to every teammate (the Vritra clause)
trigger an empowerment consumable and charge into melee on the same turn (soma before the battle)
win a run in which a storm or weather hazard field stayed active through a full boss phase, without ever leaving the field
taboos: flee or retreat out of a boss room once combat is joined (his flight after the Vritra-kill is the king's lasting shame)
leave a dammed or hoarded resource sealed behind a beaten guardian (the waters left bound)
let a rival patron's blessing be honored at his table without out-bidding or contesting it (the insecure king brooks no equal)
patron_block.blessing_style: storm-front-loaded and conditional on nerve — an opening vajra-strike buff plus rain that swells the party's shared resources; his favor surges with soma-fuelled aggression and drains the instant you flinch, flee, or let a hoarder keep the waters bound.

game_hooks: Patron + prime Forsaken candidate — the deposed Vedic king. FORSAKEN table: like his Buddhist office (buddhist_shakra_indra, the five omens of a deva's death), Puranic Indra is a chairman who has 'lost his throne a thousand times' (Govardhana humbling by Krishna; the Ahalya curse; brahmahatya-guilt flight after killing Vritra); his all-in is a bid to reclaim the mandate, and losing it can open a 'throne-vacated' stage (§5). Signature table mode = the VRITRA RELEASE: a gate-keeper boss dams a resource the whole party needs (water / loot / passage) and the discoverable win is to break the dam and RELEASE it to everyone — never a raw damage race. Soma-charge event: a pre-boss empowerment consumable that must be spent by charging in on the same turn. Insecure-king event: he sends apsara distractions (echoing his sabotage of ascetics' penances) that debuff a rival contestant's focus. Sahasraksha ('thousand-eyed') flavor for a full-map-reveal boon; Airavata the rain-elephant as a storm-field summon.
rating_notes: influence 3 — living continuous festival/folk practice (Indra Jatra, Kathmandu's biggest street festival, honoring Indra as rain and harvest god) plus his dikpala-of-the-east ritual invocation, but almost no dedicated temple cult today (a demoted king): matches the Kubera influence-3 'continuous folk invocation, thin cult' logic, below Shani-4's Shingnapur-scale daily worship and the influence-5 principal deities (Ganesha anchor). recognition 3 — the 'Hindu Zeus,' known to mythology-curious audiences (Väinämöinen / Enki anchor) but short of a Zeus/Thor household name (recognition 5). Coherent with the syncretic Buddhist office buddhist_shakra_indra (recognition 3; influence 4 there because Taishakuten/Phra In/Sakka are actively venerated across Buddhist Asia — the Hindu Indra's own living cult is thinner, hence influence 3).
sources: Rig Veda, the Indra hymns and the Vritra-slaying / soma-empowerment (Griffith tr., PD) — most-invoked Vedic deity, ~250 hymns; Vritrahan releases the waters
Mahabharata (Ganguli tr., PD) — Svarga/Amaravati, Indra at heaven's gate offering Yudhishthira paradise (Svargarohana Parva), Arjuna's divine paternity
Ramayana (Griffith tr., PD) — the Ahalya episode and Gautama's curse (source of the Sahasraksha 'thousand-eyed' epithet)
Vishnu Purana I.9 (Wilson tr., PD) — Durvasa's garland trampled by Indra's elephant and Lakshmi's departure from his heaven (myth_hindu_lakshmi_departs_heaven)
Bhagavata / Vishnu Purana — Krishna lifts Mount Govardhana and humbles Indra (the demoted-king arc)

Web verification 2026-07-19 (index-level, claims verified against the PD primaries above): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indra, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indra_Jatra (living rain-god festival), en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airavata, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indrani (consort Shachi/Indrani)
