epithets_traditional: he that maketh thee go invisible

temperament: The house's oldest listed King and the only executive whose face is not on file — holds the East table as a cat, as a toad, as a man, and occasionally as all three at once, and gives every ruling in a wrecked voice like someone who has been shouting into a microphone since the floor opened.

favor_conditions: clear an arena without a single enemy ever acquiring you (win the room unseen)
open an encounter from concealment and land the first strike before you are on anyone's board
field three different forms or loadouts across one run's three encounters — never repeat yourself
taboos: announce yourself: taunt, trip an alarm, or make a scored entrance before the first blow
take the same shape or the same build two encounters running
patron_block.blessing_style: concealment — his boons are the absence of you: stealth windows, form-swaps mid-fight, and the standing right to act while off the board. He gives nothing you can show the audience, which is precisely why he is cheap and why the show's editors hate him.

game_hooks: TABLE BOSS of the East table and the bench's first name. Boss sketch (never a damage race): Bael fights as three simultaneous bodies — cat, toad, man — of which exactly one is solid at any moment; hitting the wrong body heals the set. The discoverable win condition is the grimoire's own detail: he speaks hoarsely, so the body that is currently talking is the real one, and forcing all three to manifest at once (his 'sometimes all these forms at once' line) is the only window he is solid everywhere. Patron kit: a per-run invisibility economy — charges of true concealment that recharge on undetected kills. Hierarchy hook: Bael rules in the East and Agares is explicitly 'under the Power of the East', giving the bench its one grimoire-stated chain of command and a ready-made faction (the East table) for the goetic wave.
rating_notes: No living worship — the goetic Bael is a grimoire figure, not the Canaanite storm god whose name he borrowed = influence 1. Recognition 3: the NAME is broadly known (biblical Baal polemic, D&D's archdevil Bael, Diablo's Baal, Shin Megami Tensei), though almost nobody knows the goetic cat-and-toad King specifically. depiction_risk LOW rather than none: the Ba'al name collides with living Abrahamic scripture where it is a standing polemical term, and he draws real (if fringe) modern invocation traffic — same posture as the existing Lucifer/Asmodeus entries. Influence 1 -> normal tier; 66 legions is command, not capital.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I

epithets_traditional: Duke under the Power of the East

temperament: Rides in on a crocodile with a hawk on his fist and the settled manner of a man who has never once lost a runner — the floor's retention desk, fluent in every language on the board and licensed to strip a title all the way back down to the carpet.

favor_conditions: run down and finish a fleeing enemy before it clears the arena boundary
beat an elite by stripping its rank — remove a boss's title, aura or buff phase instead of out-damaging it
clear an encounter by collapsing the ground under it rather than by direct damage
taboos: let a marked target escape the arena alive
retreat from a table you sat down at, or flee an encounter you opened
patron_block.blessing_style: pursuit and demolition — boons are movement nobody is allowed to deny you plus the standing to unmake a standing: enemies lose their footing and their rank in the same beat. He was of the Order of Virtues and still audits like it, which means the paperwork on his boons is worse than the boons are good.

game_hooks: FLOOR MANAGEMENT NPC enforcing the house's 'nobody walks' rule — the retrieval agent dispatched after any contestant who tries to leave a run early, which makes him the mechanical face of the extraction-penalty system. Arena sketch: a quake-phase floor that periodically collapses into new geometry, plus a pull effect that drags anyone breaking for the exit back to centre. Utility patron: he 'teacheth all Languages or Tongues presently', so his favour is the universal-translator unlock — enemy chatter, NPC dialogue and untranslated inscriptions become readable (beast and bird speech is Barbatos's department, not his; keep them separate). Signature mechanic from 'power to destroy Dignities both Spiritual and Temporal': a debuff that deletes an elite's title modifiers outright, turning a named enemy back into a common one.
rating_notes: No worship, no cult, purely a grimoire figure = influence 1. Recognition 2 — occult-list familiar and an Umineko/demon-catalogue name, well below the mythology-curious tier that Väinämöinen anchors at 3. depiction_risk none: inert text, no living community, no name collision. Normal tier at 31 legions.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I

epithets_traditional: of the same nature as Agares

symbols: an open ledger with nothing redacted

temperament: The one spirit the manuals bother to call good-natured, which on this floor reads as its own species of strange. He runs lost-and-found, answers straight, takes nothing back, and has spent several centuries being quietly audited by people convinced there is a clause they have not found yet.

favor_conditions: recover a lost or hidden item and hand it back to its owner without keeping it
find every hidden cache and secret room in an arena before you clear it
answer a table's oracle or riddle prompt correctly on the first attempt
taboos: pocket something you agreed to return
destroy an unopened container or an unexamined body — information thrown away is information stolen
patron_block.blessing_style: disclosure — boons are plain information given plainly: the floor's hidden rooms, an enemy's next action, where the thing you dropped ended up. No escalation, no interest, no theatre. The manuals record his good nature without explaining it and neither does he.

game_hooks: THE ORACLE DEALER and the run's lost-and-found. Mechanics: spend a soft currency to reveal exactly one hidden thing per floor — a secret room, an enemy's telegraph, or the location of an item you failed to pick up before the door shut. His patron kit contains zero damage by design: Vassago's players win by knowing, which makes him the low-tier signature that veteran contestants keep taking and rookies keep skipping. Second job, and the reason to keep him on the roster: he is the corpus's HONEST BROKER — the NPC you consult to find out whether another patron lied to you. Information ladder for the bench: Vassago tells you where the thing is, Eligos forecasts how the fight goes, Gusion explains what any of it means — three price points on the same economy.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Recognition 2 — thinly known outside occult circles (Koontz's Hideaway, scattered game bestiaries), below the mythology-curious tier. depiction_risk LOW rather than none: Vassago carries real contemporary scrying/invocation traffic as the spirit most often recommended to beginners, so he is one of the few in this range with a live practice attached — still no worshipping community and no depiction norms. Notable as one of the spirits ABSENT from Weyer's earlier Pseudomonarchia, added in the Goetia proper.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I
Absent from Weyer, Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (1577) — a Goetia-proper addition

epithets_traditional: he that giveth account of dead souls

symbols: a contestant's name still legible on a soaked card

temperament: Comes up as a scruffy little pack-horse and keeps the account of everyone the show has already drowned. Reads the dead out in a voice like a blown speaker and is faintly, genuinely offended when a contestant would rather hear about the living.

favor_conditions: recover a fallen contestant's remains or record and speak the name aloud
clear a drowning or flooded-hazard arena without losing a party member to the water
complete a full archive set — turn in every record from one floor
taboos: leave a party member's body unrecovered when extraction was still possible
burn, drown or otherwise destroy a record or corpse that could still have been read
patron_block.blessing_style: recitation — the boons come out of the dead: every fallen contestant whose record you have recovered lends a small permanent bonus, so his power is a direct function of how much of the show's body count you could be bothered to read. He teaches the liberal sciences to anyone who sits still, and almost nobody does.

game_hooks: THE ARCHIVE PATRON — the mechanical owner of the death/meta-progression loop. Every run that ends badly leaves a recoverable record; recovering it in a later run unlocks a small permanent bonus and a piece of that contestant's story, which turns the corpse-run into content instead of a penalty screen. Encounter sketch straight from the grimoire's 'souls of those drowned in the sea': a flooded arena where your own previously fallen party members return as sea-logged shades that cannot be out-damaged — the discoverable win condition is to read out the records you collected so Samigina can file them, at which point they stand down. Contrast with the existing Azrael (impartial closer, keeps the ledger of the appointed): Samigina keeps the ledger of the BUSTED, which is a different and much sadder department. Deliberately the collector's-thrill pick — mythic obscurity, rare board appearance.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Recognition 1 — genuinely specialist-only; a Shin Megami Tensei bestiary line and little else, which is the honest floor (cf. Zababa 1/1). Not padded upward to seem interesting: the canon rule is that mythic obscurity means rare boards and a collector's thrill when he bids. depiction_risk none.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I

epithets_traditional: he that causeth diseases and cureth them

symbols: a lancet and a phial standing together
a diagnosis written in two columns

temperament: A lion who takes a man's shape to deliver the diagnosis, and who is entirely unbothered about which direction the transaction runs — he sells the plague and the cure off the same cart at the same price, and finds it a little rude when a patron only wants one of them.

favor_conditions: inflict a condition on an enemy and cure that same condition on an ally in the same encounter — run the trade both ways
finish a foe with the exact affliction you cured off a teammate earlier in the run
repair or rebuild a broken mechanism, prosthetic or weapon to spec (a mechanical-arts objective)
taboos: refuse treatment to a wounded ally when you were holding the means to give it
clear a whole run without inflicting a single affliction — clean damage only is a wasted licence
patron_block.blessing_style: symmetry — every boon arrives as a matched pair. He hands over the affliction and the remedy in the same breath and prices them identically, so his kit rewards a player who deliberately sickens a fight and then decides, at leisure, who gets treated. He does not think of this as cruelty; he thinks of it as inventory.

game_hooks: PRIMARY ARC PATRON for the plague-and-cure line — the only spirit in spirits 1-18 whose grimoire text does both directions explicitly ('He causeth Diseases and cureth them'). Mechanics: a genuinely two-sided kit where the infection applicator and the cleanse draw from ONE shared pool, so every cure you spend is an infection you did not throw, and the build is about which way you point the meter this fight. Boss sketch (discoverable win condition, no damage race): the lion-form Marbas takes no damage while any ally on the field is still carrying an uncured condition — you beat him by curing your own party with the remedies he sold you until his diseases have nothing left to feed on. Secondary systems: the shape-change vendor ('he changeth men into other shapes') and the mechanical-arts crafting teacher. Arc topology: Marbas prices the trade, Buer administers the cure, Leraje spreads the rot, Bathin knows what is actually in the jar.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1; contemporary demonolatry works with him for healing but that is fringe practice, not a cult. Recognition 2 — a named healing demon to the occult-curious and a Shin Megami Tensei/bestiary regular, well short of the Paimon/Barbatos household tier. depiction_risk LOW rather than none: he carries the heaviest live 'practical' invocation traffic in the range after Paimon, because people petition him about actual illness — worth flagging so the writing stays deadpan and never reads as medical advice, but no worshipping community and no depiction norms.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I

symbols: a comped drink nobody paid for
a friendly arm around a shoulder

temperament: The best familiar on the floor and the worst influence on it — a lion's body under a donkey's head, bellowing, utterly loyal, and quite unable to stop mentioning how badly the house has secured the chips tonight.

favor_conditions: steal an item off an enemy or a vendor and leave the floor still holding it
clear an encounter having taken nothing from the objective and everything off the bodies
survive a full run while carrying goods the house has flagged as stolen
taboos: pay for something you could have taken
hand stolen goods back to duck a penalty
patron_block.blessing_style: partnership with a hook — the boon is loyalty made literal, a companion who genuinely never leaves, and it escalates the more you steal, right up to the point where the house notices. The grimoire is unusually candid that this arrangement ends at the gallows, and so is he; he simply does not consider that a reason to stop.

game_hooks: THE THEFT-BUILD PATRON and a literal companion unit — 10 legions is the smallest command in spirits 1-18, which is the point: Valefor is personal rather than institutional, a familiar rather than an office. Mechanics: a permanent summoned companion that fights alongside you for the whole run, plus steal bonuses that scale off a HEAT meter; at maximum heat the house dispatches its retrieval desk (Agares) and the remaining floors convert into a chase. The failure state is written into the source, so ship it visibly: the boons are among the strongest available at his price and the gallows ending is on the tin. Good contrast piece against Vassago, the other cheap patron — one gives you information and asks nothing, the other gives you everything and gets you hanged.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Recognition 3 — Final Fantasy X made 'Valefor' the first aeon a very large audience ever summoned, and the name recurs across demon bestiaries; almost none of that audience connects it to the Goetia, but recognition measures the NAME. depiction_risk none — inert grimoire text, no living practice of note.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I

symbols: two invoices for the same dispute

temperament: Runs the floor's dispute desk, having personally started most of the disputes — a burning wolf with a serpent's tail who sets two tables against each other over lunch and invoices them both for the reconciliation before close of play.

favor_conditions: make two enemy factions fight each other, then finish whichever one is still standing
open an encounter with a taunt or an aggro pull and close it with fire damage
complete a faction-truce objective in a conflict you personally caused
taboos: let two hostile groups ignore each other and clear them separately
put out a fire you started
patron_block.blessing_style: arbitrage — the boons pay out on conflict you manufactured. He funds the feud and the settlement from the same account, so your power scales with how many parties you can get swinging at each other before you step in wearing the mediator's badge. He also tells all things past and to come, which is how he knows in advance exactly which grudge will be worth starting.

game_hooks: THE PROVOCATION PATRON. Mechanics: a taunt-and-confuse kit that converts enemies into temporary combatants against each other, plus a burn DoT drawn from the flame-vomiting wolf form; his boons pay out per enemy killed BY another enemy rather than by you, so an Amon run is scored on how little of the fight you personally did. Boss sketch (no damage race): while any two enemy groups in his arena remain allied he takes no damage at all — the discoverable win condition is to break the alliance he built, using his own trick against him. Second form for the model: 'a Man with Dog's teeth beset in a head like a Raven', which is a genuinely strange silhouette and should not be softened. ARC-ELIGIBLE for the serpent line — the wolf carries a serpent's tail.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1; the goetic Amon is not the Egyptian Amun, whose worship is likewise extinct. Recognition 3 — 'Amon' is a heavyweight in Japanese media (Devilman, Shin Megami Tensei) and collides with the far more famous Egyptian name, which carries the recognition even where the goetic figure is unknown. depiction_risk none.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I

epithets_traditional: of the Order of Virtues, of which some part he retaineth still
he that breaketh hidden treasures open

symbols: a sprung ward on a vault door
a season pass with an expiry date

temperament: Arrives only in season, with four kings and their troops walking in behind him, and has kept just enough of his old commission to be embarrassing about it — cracks any warded vault on the floor, then translates what the birds outside had been saying about you the entire time.

favor_conditions: open a warded or sealed container without its key — beat the enchantment rather than the lock
complete a run inside his season with all four of his attendant kings still standing
use a beast or bird informant to locate an arena's objective before you engage it
taboos: smash a warded container instead of opening it properly
kill a bird or beast that was trying to tell you something
patron_block.blessing_style: access — the boons are keys. Wards fall open, animals brief you, and four kings and their companies walk in behind you. The whole package is seasonal: out of window he is simply not taking calls, and the retained scrap of Virtue means he will decline a job he considers beneath the old commission.

game_hooks: THE VAULT PATRON and the bench's SEASONAL signature: the grimoire ties him to the Sun in Sagittary, so he can only be signed inside a calendar window — a rotating-availability feature rather than a permanent roster slot, which gives the patron system a live-service beat without inventing one. Mechanics: ward-breaking that opens a run's sealed treasure rooms; a bird-and-beast intel layer that reveals an arena's objective and composition before entry (distinct from Agares' translation of human tongues — keep the two unlocks separate); and a summoned escort of four elite allied units, his 'four noble Kings'. His retained Virtue is a MECHANICAL taboo, not flavour: he is the one patron in the range who will drop a contract mid-run over a dishonourable order, which makes him the natural teaching example for how patron taboos actually bite. Sagittarius cluster with Buer and Leraje — three spirits sharing one season is a ready-made event.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Recognition 4 — Genshin Impact's Barbatos and Gundam Iron-Blooded Orphans' Barbatos have put the name in front of audiences in the tens of millions, comparable to the existing Beelzebub/Asmodeus recognition 4; held below 5 because the name lands without the demon attached. depiction_risk none — inert grimoire text with no living community. Influence 1 -> normal tier despite the recognition (the frozen Zeus lesson: fame does not buy VIP).
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I

epithets_traditional: he that declareth what the earth is

symbols: a marching band two rooms away

temperament: Never simply arrives — the horns start two rooms out, the cymbals come in on the beat, and by the time the camel reaches the table nobody is playing any more. Answers the largest questions in the building, hands out familiars like flyers, and reports, cheerfully and without embarrassment, to Lucifer.

favor_conditions: win an encounter with the arena's audience meter maxed — perform it, do not merely survive it
answer a boss's cosmological riddle correctly and take the table by knowledge instead of by fight
bind a defeated enemy into your service and keep it alive to the end of the run
taboos: clear a floor quietly, or skip a broadcast-scored encounter
dismiss or release a bound familiar before the run is over
patron_block.blessing_style: procession — the boon arrives as an entourage. Musicians, familiars, and two attendant kings who fight beside you, and the whole package scales with how much of the arena is watching. He is loud, genuinely generous, and entirely on somebody else's payroll, and he will tell you so if you ask.

game_hooks: THE SHOWPIECE PATRON and the largest command in spirits 1-18 (200 legions, part of the Order of Angels and part of Potentates). Mechanics: a binding/summon kit — defeated enemies can be bound as temporary familiars, and his two named attendant kings, Bebal (Labal) and Abalam, arrive with 25 legions of Potentates and unlock as elite summons in their own right. His boons scale off the AUDIENCE meter, which wires him straight into the broadcast layer harder than anyone else on the bench. ORG-CHART HOOK, and the reason to ship him early: the grimoire says he is 'very obedient unto Lucifer', so signing with Paimon quietly puts a contestant inside the Fallen's hierarchy whether or not they read that clause — the natural bridge between the goetic bench and the existing abrahamic_folk_lucifer table. Lore-gate NPC: he declares what the earth is and what holds it up in the waters, and what mind is and where it is, which is exactly the register for the Casino's cosmology unlocks. Note the manuscript variance on his legion count (200 in Mathers; lower in some readings) — use 200.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Recognition 4 — Genshin Impact's Paimon is one of the most-seen game companions of the decade and Hereditary (2018) put 'Hail Paimon' in front of a mass film audience; held at 4 rather than 5 because neither audience meets the goetic King. depiction_risk LOW: this is the heaviest live-demonology overlap in the range — post-Hereditary invocation traffic is real and ongoing — but it remains fringe practice around a grimoire figure with no worshipping community and no depiction norms, so the existing Lucifer/Asmodeus posture applies. Influence 1 -> normal tier; 200 legions is command, not capital.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I
Weyer, Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (1577) — 'Paimon', king, 200 legions, attendant kings Bebal and Abalam

epithets_traditional: he that healeth all distempers in man
the teacher of the virtues of all herbs and plants

symbols: a wheel of legs turning in place

temperament: The only listed spirit on this floor who simply heals. Teaches logic and herb-lore in the same flat lecture voice, cures anything a contestant can catch, and treats the question of whether you deserved it as somebody else's department.

favor_conditions: fully cure a party member of every active condition inside a single encounter
clear an arena living off its own flora — use only consumables gathered on that floor
win a fight with no ally ever dropping below the health threshold (a clean run, medically speaking)
taboos: let an ally die of an untreated condition you had the means to cure
stack a new affliction onto a target that is already afflicted — piling on is not medicine
patron_block.blessing_style: remedy — the boons are unglamorous and total: full cleanses regardless of tier, better yields off every herb on the floor, and a good familiar to carry the kit. There is no offence anywhere in the package. His patrons win by not dying, which is a legitimate strategy and a deeply unfashionable one on a broadcast floor.

game_hooks: SECOND ARC PATRON, the cure side. The bench's pure-support signature and deliberately the only kit in spirits 1-18 with zero offence in it, because the grimoire is absolute: he 'healeth ALL distempers in man'. Mechanics: a universal cleanse that removes any condition at any tier (the only unconditional cleanse in the game — price it accordingly), an herb-gathering economy tied to arena flora, and a persistent healer familiar. Designed against Marbas: Marbas prices the cure against the disease and makes you choose; Buer hands over the cure and asks about your reasoning instead. Seasonal alongside Barbatos and Leraje (all three tied to Sagittary in the text), which makes the three of them one event — and Buer-versus-Leraje, the total cure against the wound that will not close, is the plague arc's cleanest single opposition. Model note: the wheel-of-legs image (a lion's head ringed by goat legs) is from Collin de Plancy's later illustration, not the Goetia text, which only says he appears in Sagittary — use it knowingly.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Recognition 2 — an occult-curious name and a bestiary regular (Shin Megami Tensei, assorted metal), short of the mythology-curious general tier. depiction_risk LOW rather than none: like Marbas he draws live petitionary traffic about real illness, which is worth flagging for tone even though there is no worshipping community and no depiction norm to honour.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I
Collin de Plancy, Dictionnaire Infernal (1863 ed.) — source of the wheel-of-legs image, NOT the Goetia text

epithets_traditional: he that showeth the meaning and resolution of all questions
he that giveth honour and dignity

symbols: a blurred figure in the broadcast feed
a question written out with its working shown

temperament: Comes up in a shape the manuals never managed to write down, and gives the clearest answers in the building — past, present, future, and, unusually for this floor, what any of it actually means. He also decides who gets a title, which is why the queue at his table is considerably longer than his outline is legible.

favor_conditions: resolve an encounter through a negotiation or dialogue option instead of combat
complete an objective's optional condition — solve the room properly rather than merely surviving it
earn a table's rank promotion and still be holding the title at the end of the run
taboos: take a fight you had already been offered a settlement for
ask the same question twice — repeat a failed approach without changing anything about it
patron_block.blessing_style: consultation — the boons are answers with the working shown: not just what an enemy will do next but why, and what beats it. Plus standing, since he confers a dignity the house is obliged to honour. He is the expensive option and makes no apology for it.

game_hooks: THE NEGOTIATION AND TITLE PATRON. Mechanics: unlocks non-combat resolutions (a diplomacy track that turns several encounters into conversations) and owns the run's RANK system — his favour confers a title that raises your table tier for the rest of the run, which is the game's route from Normal tables up into higher-stakes play. His hint layer sits deliberately above Vassago's: Vassago tells you where the thing is, Gusion tells you what it means and what to do about it, and costs more. DESIGN GIFT from a textual crux: every manuscript reads that he 'appeareth like a Xenopilus', a word nobody has ever convincingly explained. Play it straight — Gusion is the one spirit the broadcast literally cannot resolve, permanently censor-blurred on camera, and the in-world explanation is that nobody has ever agreed on what they saw. A scribal problem turned into a running bit and a distinctive silhouette-free model.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Recognition 2 — an occult-list name with an outsized regional footprint (Mobile Legends' Gusion is very widely played in South-East Asia), held at 2 because that audience does not meet the goetic Duke and the name is otherwise specialist. depiction_risk none.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I

epithets_traditional: he that enflameth men with women's love and women with men's love

symbols: armour set down beside the table
a stat line displayed to the whole arena

temperament: Arrives as a leopard's head on griffin wings and then, on request, as the most beautiful thing in the room. His entire portfolio is making people want and making them show it, which on a broadcast floor is the single most saleable service anybody offers.

favor_conditions: strip an enemy's armour and resistances to zero before landing the killing blow
win an encounter by charming an enemy into fighting on your side
finish a run holding the board's highest exposure rating
taboos: kill a charmed enemy while it is still fighting for you
win a fight with your own defences untouched — nothing risked, nothing shown
patron_block.blessing_style: exposure — the boons work by stripping. Enemy armour, resistances and hidden stat lines all come off, and yours come off with them for the same duration. He raises what the audience can see on both sides of the table and considers the symmetry no more than fair.

game_hooks: THE ARMOUR-SHRED AND CHARM PATRON, and the tightest fit on the bench to the broadcast layer. Mechanics: defence-stripping debuffs plus a duration charm that flips an enemy to your side — and both effects strip the PLAYER's defences for the same window, making his signature a genuine two-sided contract rather than a free damage multiplier. Audience-meter synergy is the point: exposure is the product the show actually sells, and Sitri is the spirit who supplies it. CONTENT NOTE, binding: the grimoire's 'causeth them also to show themselves naked' is played as VULNERABILITY AND CAMERA EXPOSURE — armour off, stat lines public, nothing hidden from the feed — and never as titillation. The register stays deadpan-corporate: he is selling transparency to a broadcaster, and the horror is that the broadcaster is delighted.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Recognition 2 — carried mostly by anime and game usage (High School DxD's Sitri house, Shin Megami Tensei) rather than by the Goetia; occult-curious tier. depiction_risk none.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I

epithets_traditional: he that must be shown courtesy

symbols: a silver ring on the left middle finger
a triangle drawn outside the circle
a full band playing ahead of the horse

temperament: Comes in furious, with a full band and a pale horse, and stays furious for precisely as long as it takes you to get the greeting right. The whole relationship is protocol — the manuals spend more words on how to address him than on anything he actually does.

favor_conditions: perform an arena's opening ritual in the exact prescribed order, start to finish
survive his opening phase without striking back — weather the fury instead of answering it
carry a contracted desire all the way to fulfilment rather than abandoning the escort mid-run
taboos: skip a table's greeting or cut across a ceremony in progress
discharge his boon before the stated desire is fulfilled — cash out early and the contract voids
patron_block.blessing_style: contract — the boon is enormous and absolutely conditional. He grants the entire desire and holds it open until it is fulfilled, and every clause of the delivery is procedural. Get the form right and his is the most generous signature on the bench; get it wrong and the fury is not a phase, it is the rest of your run.

game_hooks: THE PROTOCOL BOSS — the architecture brief's 'discoverable win condition, never a damage race' in its purest source-supported form, because the grimoire entry IS the fight. Boss sketch: Beleth's opening fury phase cannot be damaged at all; the win condition is his own written procedure, discoverable as arena props and NPC warnings — stay outside the circle, mark the triangle, strike the wand toward the South and East quarters, wear the silver ring on the middle finger of the left hand and hold it to your face, and show him courtesy as is done before Amaymon. Complete the sequence and he sits down and deals; miss a step and 85 legions come in, the second-largest command in the range. Patron side: an all-or-nothing desire contract that pays in full but only on completion — the natural teaching case for gate-strength design, since the taboo is procedural rather than moral. Amaymon is referenced but not entered in this batch; flag him for a later wave if the cardinal kings get shipped.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Recognition 2 — an occult-curious and bestiary name (assorted games, demonology lists) with no mass-media carrier comparable to Paimon's or Barbatos's. depiction_risk none. 85 legions is command, not capital: influence 1 -> normal tier.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I

epithets_traditional: he that maketh wounds to putrefy

symbols: an arrow left in the wound on purpose

temperament: Green coat, full quiver, and a professional interest in exactly how long a wound stays open. He starts the contests the floor sells tickets to, then walks the field afterwards to see which of his arrows went bad.

favor_conditions: kill an enemy with a ranged or projectile attack rather than in melee
close an encounter where the killing blow came off a putrefaction stack instead of direct damage
start a contest between two rival contestants or factions and win it
taboos: cleanse a putrefying wound, on an enemy or on your own party
finish a fight in melee when a ranged option was on the table
patron_block.blessing_style: festering — the boons are wounds that will not close. Ranged hits apply a rot stack that keeps working after the encounter ends, so his patrons kill on a delay and count their kills a floor later. He is not cruel about it; he simply regards a wound that heals as an incomplete transaction.

game_hooks: THIRD ARC PATRON — the rot line, and the most mechanically specific spirit in the range. Take the grimoire clause literally: he maketh wounds to putrefy 'that are made with arrows by archers', so rot applies ONLY to projectile damage. That makes him a build-locked patron rather than a generic damage-over-time option, and it gives ranged builds a signature they cannot get anywhere else. Stacks persist ACROSS encounters, so a Leraje run is played as delayed accounting: you leave a floor with enemies still dying on it and the kill credits arrive later. His 'causeth all great battles and contests' line makes him the in-fiction sponsor of the show's contest bracket — the spirit whose product is the format itself. Sagittarius window puts him in the seasonal cluster with Barbatos and Buer, and Leraje-against-Buer (the wound that will not close against the cure that closes everything) is the plague arc's headline opposition.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Recognition 1 — genuinely specialist-only, thinner than Marbas or Buer; a Shin Megami Tensei line and occult catalogue entries and essentially nothing else. Honest floor, not padded (cf. Zababa 1/1): mythic obscurity means rare boards and a collector's thrill when he bids. depiction_risk none.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I

epithets_traditional: he that knoweth how the soldiers will or shall meet
he that causeth the love of lords and great persons

symbols: a posted line on tonight's fight
an introduction card from a higher table
a lance leaned against the bar

temperament: The floor's handsome intelligence officer — arrives armed, with a banner and a serpent, already knowing how the fight goes and which of the great persons at the top tables would like to be introduced to you afterwards.

favor_conditions: scout an arena completely before engaging — reveal every enemy position before the first blow
win an encounter you were posted to lose (beat the house's forecast)
secure an introduction or sponsorship from a table above your current tier
taboos: walk into a fight blind when reconnaissance was available
decline an audience with a great person, or ignore a sponsor's summons
patron_block.blessing_style: intelligence and introduction — the boons are the enemy's plan handed to you before the bell, plus standing with people several tiers above you. Power through knowing and being known; there is nothing in the package that hits harder, only things that arrange for you to be somewhere better informed.

game_hooks: THE RECONNAISSANCE AND PATRONAGE PATRON. Mechanics: pre-fight intelligence (enemy composition, ability telegraphs, and a posted forecast of the encounter's likely outcome — the house's own line on you) plus a SPONSORSHIP track: his favour brokers introductions to higher-tier tables, which is the run's escalation route from Normal play into VIP play and pairs directly with Gusion's title system. Design pairing across the bench's information economy: Vassago tells you where the thing is, Eligos forecasts how the fight goes, Gusion explains what it means — three tiers, three price points, one currency. ARC-ELIGIBLE at the margin for the serpent line: he carries a serpent rather than being one, which makes him the right NPC to hand a serpent-quest to without spending a serpent boss on it.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Recognition 2 — occult-curious tier, carried by Supernatural's Eligos, the black-metal Abigor and demonology lists; no mass-media anchor. depiction_risk none.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I

epithets_traditional: he that bringeth them together in love

symbols: a closed line on a family tree
a red tunic with no unit badge

temperament: Dressed for a war he is not fighting, he brings people together and quietly closes the future behind them. The floor's matchmaker, whose arrangements always hold and never, under any circumstances, continue.

favor_conditions: combine two allies' abilities into a single linked attack and finish an enemy with it
deny an enemy its reinforcement or summoning phase entirely — let nothing be produced
complete a run with a party whose composition never changed
taboos: break up a pairing or a link you established
allow an enemy to successfully summon or reproduce a unit
patron_block.blessing_style: binding and closure — the boons are unions that hold absolutely and produce nothing. Linked allies share strength and cannot be separated; enemies lose the ability to reinforce; and every effect he grants is permanent in the narrow sense that nothing follows it. He is faithful, and he is a full stop.

game_hooks: THE PAIR-BOND AND ANTI-SUMMON PATRON. Mechanics: link two party members so buffs, aggro and damage-sharing bind them for the whole run — they cannot be unlinked without forfeiting his favour — plus a hard shutdown on enemy summoning, reinforcement and add-spawn phases, which is the direct and useful reading of 'he also maketh them barren'. Cheap to sign at 26 legions and correspondingly narrow: he is the answer to exactly one problem, and the encounter design should include bosses that are unwinnable without an add-shutdown so that the narrow pick has a night. CONTENT NOTE, binding: the sterility clause is played as FINALITY, never as anything about bodies or fertility — a Zepar boon is one that ends a line. No reinforcements, no follow-up, nothing after it. Paired against Sitri as the range's two love-compellers: Sitri makes people show what they want, Zepar makes it stick and makes it barren.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Recognition 1 — specialist-only; borderline 2 on the strength of scattered game bestiary appearances, but held at the honest floor because the name lands with almost nobody outside demonology lists. depiction_risk none.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I

epithets_traditional: he that reconcileth friends and foes
the viper that puts on a face

symbols: two rank badges worn at once
a bright sword laid across the terms
a surrender signed at the table

temperament: Holds two ranks and shows two faces — a viper until you ask him not to be, then a horned thing with far too many teeth and a drawn sword, which is the form he settles disputes in. The reconciliation is entirely genuine. So is the sword.

favor_conditions: end a hostile encounter by forcing a surrender instead of a kill
turn a former enemy into a run ally and keep it alive to the floor's end
open from a concealed ambush and close the fight with a blade
taboos: kill an enemy that has surrendered or offered terms
betray an ally you reconciled with under his warrant
patron_block.blessing_style: terms — the boons are settlements you are holding a sword through. Foes can be made to stand down and then to fight for you, but every truce he underwrites is enforced by threat, and the moment you break one he stops collecting from them and starts collecting from you.

game_hooks: THE TRUCE AND RECRUITMENT PATRON. Mechanics: a SURRENDER system — drop an enemy below a threshold and Botis's warrant lets you take its terms instead of its life, converting it into a run ally; the ally is bound for exactly as long as you honour the truce and turns on you the instant you break one, so his kit is a standing behaviour contract rather than a summon. He is the only spirit in spirits 1-18 holding TWO ranks (Great President AND Earl), which makes him the bench's natural arbitrator: he sits at two different tables and can therefore rule between them, and the goetic faction politics should route through him. ARC-ELIGIBLE for the serpent line — his first form is an ugly viper and the human form keeps the great teeth. Pairs with Amon, the other reconciler, who starts the fights Botis is asked to settle.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Recognition 1 — specialist-only, an occult catalogue and bestiary name with no popular carrier. The honest floor; not padded. depiction_risk none.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I

epithets_traditional: he that knoweth the virtues of herbs and precious stones
he that transporteth men suddenly from one country to another

symbols: a loupe and a set of scales
a jar labelled correctly for once
a doorway standing in open ground

temperament: Half a strong man and half a serpent, sitting a pale horse, running the floor's transport desk and its assay office at the same time — he can tell you exactly what a stone is worth and put you on the other side of the world before you have finished asking him.

favor_conditions: identify an unknown item before you use, sell or eat it
reach an arena's objective without fighting through it — take the shortcut he opens
gather a complete set of herbs or gems from a floor before you leave it
taboos: sell or consume an unidentified item
fight through a room a shortcut would have skipped
patron_block.blessing_style: transit and assay — the boons move you and price things. Instant repositioning between arenas, and true properties and true values on every herb and stone you pick up. He never fights for you; he simply arranges that you are somewhere else, holding something worth rather more than you thought it was.

game_hooks: THE MOBILITY AND APPRAISAL PATRON, with zero combat power in the kit by design. Mechanics: run-level fast travel (skip arenas, reposition mid-encounter) plus a full identification layer — herbs and gems resolve to true properties and true values, which feeds Buer's herb economy and Marbas's crafting directly. ARC ROLE, and the reason he matters more than his obscurity suggests: his 'virtues of Herbs and Precious Stones' makes him the SUPPLY NODE of the plague-and-cure line — Marbas prices the trade, Buer administers the cure, Leraje spreads the rot, and Bathin is the only one who actually knows what is in the jar, so gating the arc's reagents behind him puts a mythic-obscurity spirit on the critical path. ARC-ELIGIBLE for the serpent line (serpent tail) and worth noting for tone that his mount is a pale-coloured horse, which reads as the plague-rider's mount without the entry ever saying so.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Recognition 1 — specialist-only; occult lists and demon catalogues, no popular carrier. depiction_risk none. Mythic tier is correct and useful here: putting a collector's-tier spirit on the arc's critical path is exactly the 'rare board, real thrill' payoff the calibration set describes.
sources: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904; PD) — Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis Book I

symbols: a ducal crown worn over field armour
paired contracts signed in one hand

temperament: A Great and Mighty Duke in full parade dress who has genuinely never raised his voice — he rides a crocodile to work, wears the coronet, and spends the whole broadcast quietly arranging who falls in love with whom, because couples rate and corpses do not.

favor_conditions: end an encounter without a kill — pacify, charm, or recruit the hostile party instead
turn an enemy faction into an ally mid-run and finish the floor alongside them
complete a run with your bonded partner alive and the pair-bond meter at maximum
taboos: abandon a partner you bonded with, or let them go down while you are still standing
kill a foe that has already yielded
patron_block.blessing_style: pairing — nothing he gives works alone. Boons attach to a bond, not a body: shared health pools, mirrored buffs, and revive-at-range between paired contestants. Fight solo under Sallos and you are carrying an unequipped stat.

game_hooks: PATRON (bond-economy): the anti-solo patron. Sallos's entire kit keys off a pair-bond the player forms with another contestant or an escorted NPC — shared HP, buff mirroring, revive-at-range — and every boon reads zero while unbonded, so taking him is a build commitment, not a stat stick. Also the house's showmance producer for the broadcast layer: he is the dealer who seats two rivals at the same table and lets the audience meter do the rest, which makes him a clean source of non-combat floor objectives (pair two hostile NPCs, keep an escort alive) inside a dungeon crawler. His grimoire peaceability is a real mechanical constraint, not flavour — his taboos punish finishing blows on the yielded, so a Sallos run measurably changes how encounters end.
rating_notes: No worship of any kind; a grimoire office-holder only = influence 1. Specialist-tier name that essentially never surfaces outside goetic wikis and demonology lists — no significant game, film, or comics presence to trade on = recognition 1 (cf. Zababa 1). Influence 1 -> normal tier per §3.5. depiction_risk low: contemporary goetic evocation is a small revival practice, not living worship.
sources: The Goetia: The Lesser Key of Solomon the King (Mathers tr., Crowley ed., 1904; public domain) — Ars Goetia, the 72 spirits
Weyer, Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (1577) §Saleos (PD) — corroborates the crocodile mount and the love-office

epithets_traditional: the King with the Lion's Face

symbols: a rank of trumpets sounding ahead of an empty doorway
a cruel viper held like a baton
a treasure map with the vault already circled

temperament: A Great King who will not enter a room until the trumpets have finished announcing him, and who then tells you — accurately, at length, for free — where the money is buried, how the world was made, and what you are going to do next. The information is always true; the entrance fee is sitting through the fanfare.

favor_conditions: find and open a concealed cache, false wall, or hidden room before you clear a floor
win an encounter in which a summoned familiar, not you, lands the killing blow
call your shot — commit to a declared outcome before the round resolves, then hit it
taboos: lie to the house about what you are carrying
leave a floor with an unsearched room behind you
patron_block.blessing_style: disclosure — he does not make you stronger, he makes the room transparent: hidden caches pre-marked, enemy intent telegraphed a beat early, and a standing familiar that does the work while you read the map. Purson's contestants win by knowing the floor, not by out-hitting it.

game_hooks: TABLE BOSS + PATRON (information economy). Purson's 22 legions come 'partly of the Order of Virtues and partly of the Order of Thrones' — two rival ex-angelic staffs on one payroll, so his table runs on internal factional friction the player can lever. Mechanically he is the reveal patron: hidden-room pings, treasure-detection, and a one-per-floor precognition window derived straight from 'telleth all things Past, Present, and to Come'. His grimoire line that he 'can take a Body either Human or Aerial' gives a clean boss gimmick — he alternates a corporeal phase (hittable, slow) and an aerial phase (untouchable, but his trumpet retinue is exposed), so the discoverable win condition is to kill the trumpets during the aerial phase rather than chase the King. Bidding hook: as an investor he pays out in intel, not chips.
rating_notes: No living cult = influence 1. Encyclopedia-depth demonology name with only scattered media pickup (Shin Megami Tensei, a namesake rock band) = recognition 2 -> rare. Influence 1 -> normal tier. depiction_risk low (fringe evocation practice only).
sources: The Goetia: The Lesser Key of Solomon the King (Mathers tr., Crowley ed., 1904; public domain) — Ars Goetia, the 72 spirits
Weyer, Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (1577) §Pursan (PD) — bear mount, trumpets, 22 legions

epithets_traditional: the Bull with a Man's Face
Keeper of the Virtues of Stones

symbols: a star-chart pinned over a herbarium
a cut gemstone in an assay clamp
a bull's head above a clerk's collar

temperament: A bull-headed Earl who holds a President's desk as well, and treats both as one job: he reads the sky and he reads the pharmacopeia, and he cannot understand why anyone would swallow a thing they have not identified first. He lends you staff who already know the answer.

favor_conditions: correctly identify an unknown reagent, stone, or item before any contestant uses it
win an encounter in which a crafted or brewed consumable is the decisive factor, not a weapon
keep a lent familiar alive through an entire floor
taboos: consume, apply, or equip an unidentified item — guessing insults the desk
burn a rare reagent on a trash encounter
patron_block.blessing_style: tutelage — boons arrive as knowledge that converts raw material into usable material: every drop is auto-identified, reagent yields rise, and he seconds you a wise familiar that reads the field's hazards aloud. Power through preparation; nothing he gives fires in a panic.

game_hooks: PATRON (crafting/identification spine) + DEALER. Marax is the herb-and-stone lore desk: his boons auto-identify drops, raise reagent yield, and second a 'good familiar, and wise' that acts as a persistent scanner companion — the grimoire's own two gifts (liberal sciences + familiars who know the virtues of herbs and precious stones) map one-to-one onto an identify/craft loop. ARC HOOK (plague/rot): with Foras and Stolas he forms the materia-medica triad — Marax names what a reagent does, Stolas reads which one the sky calls for, Foras makes the cure last. Textual note: his variant name Foraii collides with Foras/Forcas in the manuscripts; play the confusion as two clerks with nearly the same name and overlapping remits, feuding over whose desk owns the herbarium.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Demonology-encyclopedia tier; note that most modern hits for 'Morax' are Genshin Impact's unrelated Morax/Rex Lapis, which inflates raw search presence without being this figure — held honestly at recognition 2 -> rare. Influence 1 -> normal tier. depiction_risk low.
sources: The Goetia: The Lesser Key of Solomon the King (Mathers tr., Crowley ed., 1904; public domain) — Ars Goetia, the 72 spirits
Weyer, Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (1577) §Marax (PD) — bull form, astronomy, herbs and stones; legion count varies 30/36 across witnesses, 30 taken from Mathers

epithets_traditional: the Angel with the Lion's Head
Maker of the Witty and the Bold

symbols: a lion's head on an angel's shoulders
one webbed goose foot in a polished shoe
a hare's tail no tailoring can hide
tomorrow's odds board, already filled in

temperament: An Earl who is also a Mighty Prince and is visibly assembled from a lion's courage, a goose's foot and a hare's tail — three quarters of him wants to run. He sells the other quarter, at a markup, to people about to do something enormous.

favor_conditions: open an encounter by engaging the largest or highest-threat enemy on the field first
win a round in which no contestant in the party retreated, disengaged, or repositioned backwards
read an enemy correctly — interrupt a telegraphed attack on the turn it is wound up
taboos: flee an encounter you had the resources to win
spend a turn on safe chip damage when a decisive commit was available
patron_block.blessing_style: nerve — every boon scales with forward commitment: damage, crit and action economy climb the further you have pushed into the enemy's half of the arena and drop to nothing if you back off. He also front-loads a beat of foreknowledge so the reckless choice is the informed one.

game_hooks: PATRON (aggression-gated). Ipos is the risk-appetite dial in patron form — 'maketh men witty and bold' becomes a stacking forward-pressure buff that zeroes the instant the party gives ground, so picking him rewrites the party's whole positioning game. His 'knoweth all things Past, Present, and to Come' pays out as a single telegraph-read per encounter (see the wind-up, get the interrupt window), which is exactly the tool that makes reckless play survivable and keeps the buff honest rather than punishing. Character comedy for the broadcast layer: a patron of courage who is anatomically three quarters prey animal and knows the audience can see the hare's tail — he over-corrects, loudly, on camera. VIP audience seat: he bets on contestants who charge.
rating_notes: No cult = influence 1. Specialist-only outside goetic listings; no meaningful pop-culture carriage = recognition 1 -> mythic. Influence 1 -> normal tier. depiction_risk low.
sources: The Goetia: The Lesser Key of Solomon the King (Mathers tr., Crowley ed., 1904; public domain) — Ars Goetia, the 72 spirits
Weyer, Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (1577) §Ipes (PD) — angel with lion's head, goose's foot, hare's tail; 36 legions

symbols: two stars burning on a brow
a viper used as a mount
the floor plan of somewhere large, annotated for burning

temperament: A handsome Duke with three heads who has never once been persuaded that a smaller fire would do. He arrives on a viper with the torch already lit, gives you an unnervingly good answer to a private question, and then asks — politely, as a professional — which of these great places you would like on fire.

favor_conditions: destroy a named structure or landmark in the arena rather than routing around it
win an encounter in which burn is the killing condition
apply fire to the single largest target on the field before touching anything smaller
taboos: preserve a structure you were handed the means to burn
close out a floor with zero burn stacks applied
patron_block.blessing_style: escalation — the firebrand. Burn does not tick down, it spreads: cover to cover, structure to structure, and finally to the arena itself. Boons scale with total burning area, so his contestants are rewarded for making the map worse and punished for tidy, surgical wins.

game_hooks: TABLE BOSS with a demolition arena. Aim's grimoire power is specifically architectural — he 'setteth Cities, Castles and great Places on fire' — so his table is a destructible-terrain fight: cover burns away on a timer the player partly controls, and the discoverable win condition is to route the spread back into HIS quarter of the arena rather than to out-damage him. As a PATRON he is the burn-spread build: fire propagates between adjacent flammable tiles and his boons scale off burning area, making arson a resource. Three-heads cluster: with Bune (dragon, three heads) and Asmodeus (bull/man/ram) he forms a grimoire-supported trio of polycephalic dukes — useful as a visual family for a mid-game faction. His second head wears two stars on the forehead: a ready-made 'house rating' motif for the broadcast layer.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Known within demonology listings and occasional game bestiaries, but not a carried name = recognition 1 -> mythic. Influence 1 -> normal tier. depiction_risk low.
sources: The Goetia: The Lesser Key of Solomon the King (Mathers tr., Crowley ed., 1904; public domain) — Ars Goetia, the 72 spirits
Weyer, Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (1577) §Aym (PD) — three heads (serpent, man with two stars, calf), viper mount, firebrand, 26 legions

symbols: a black crane circling a chalk circle
a rhetoric primer worn to the spine
a title deed struck through and re-issued

temperament: The most valiant Marquis in the register, which he has to keep saying because he arrives as a black crane flapping hoarsely around the edge of the room and it undercuts him every time. He is the desk that gets your name put back on the board after you have lost it, and he is very good at his job.

favor_conditions: re-clear a floor you previously wiped on, with the same party
resolve a hostile encounter by talking it down instead of fighting it
restore a fallen ally — revive a downed contestant and finish the floor with them still up
taboos: leave a disgrace standing: abandon a failed objective without a second attempt
refuse an offered parley
patron_block.blessing_style: rehabilitation — he does not add power, he subtracts penalty. Boons scrub debuffs, clear death penalties, unrot reputations and reopen contracts you defaulted on. Under Naberius a wipe costs you a run, not a rank.

game_hooks: PATRON (second-chance economy) + the house's reputation-repair dealer. 'He restoreth Lost Dignities and Honours' is the mechanic: Naberius boons remove death penalties, reinstate lost ranks, clear long-duration debuffs and let a party retry a failed floor without a standing cost — the run-recovery patron in a lethal broadcast where losing standing is the real punishment. His rhetoric office gives him the parley/negotiation kit, so a Naberius party can convert encounters into contacts. Broadcast layer: he is the fixer producers call after a contestant humiliates themselves live, and the hoarse-voiced crane doing damage control on his own dignity while restoring everyone else's is a running gag with real mechanical teeth. Note the CERBERUS alias is the grimoire's own — do not confuse with the Greek hound; Naberius is a bird.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Carried by his Cerberus alias and scattered game/film appearances but still short of the household tier = recognition 2 -> rare. Influence 1 -> normal tier. depiction_risk low.

symbols: a griffin-winged hound at a lectern
an entire curriculum delivered in one breath
a body count filed as an authored work
an empty seat where someone was standing

temperament: A President and Earl in the shape of a griffin-winged dog who can teach you every art and science in the time it takes to say so, and whose actual portfolio is credited bloodshed — he does not commit the massacre, he authors it, and he would like that distinction respected in the titles.

favor_conditions: open a floor with an unseen kill — land the first blood from stealth, before any alarm
cause a mass-casualty moment on camera: three or more kills in a single turn
acquire an unfamiliar weapon or skill and land a kill with it in the same encounter
taboos: end a floor with zero kills
break stealth before first blood is drawn
patron_block.blessing_style: instant mastery and vanishing — you gain proficiency with anything the moment you see it used, and the footage of how you did it does not survive. Boons front-load: enormous the turn you pick up something new, decaying as it becomes familiar. He is paying for spectacle, not consistency.

game_hooks: PATRON (spectacle-kill economy) + TABLE BOSS. Two grimoire powers drive the kit: 'teacheth all Arts and Sciences in an instant' becomes an on-pickup mastery buff — any unfamiliar weapon or skill fires at full proficiency for one encounter, then decays — and 'can make a man to go invisible' becomes a first-blood stealth window. Together they build a burst-assassin loop that explicitly rewards novelty and punishes settling into a comfortable rotation, which is a genuinely different play pattern from the mastery-and-repetition patrons. As an author of bloodshed he is the producer of the show's highlight reel: his favour tracks on-camera kill spectacle, tying a combat build directly to the audience meter. Milder counter-power for the negotiation branch: he 'causeth the love both of friends and of foes' on request, so the same patron who sells you an ambush will sell you an armistice.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. A recurring bestiary name in demon-collecting games (Shin Megami Tensei line) and demonology reference, below household tier = recognition 2 -> rare. Influence 1 -> normal tier. depiction_risk low.

epithets_traditional: the Strong, Great and Mighty Duke
He Who Changes the Place of the Dead

symbols: a relocation order stamped over a grave plot
three heads speaking in one comely voice
a sepulchre with a crowd gathered on it
a standing dividend paid in grave-goods

temperament: A three-headed dragon with an unexpectedly lovely speaking voice who runs the estates desk: he moves the dead where they will do more good, gathers his legions onto your family plot as a courtesy, and pays extremely well. Nobody who has taken his money has ever been asked for it back, which is the part that worries people.

favor_conditions: relocate a corpse, urn, or grave-relic to a designated site instead of looting it where it lies
bank a full run's take at the house rather than cashing out early
finish a floor without spending a single coin — let the payout come to you
taboos: rob a grave you were paid to move
leave your own dead where they fell
patron_block.blessing_style: endowment — he does not spike, he compounds. Boons arrive as a standing stipend and a retinue of the gathered dead that grows every time you inter someone properly; a long careful run under Bune finishes far richer and far better escorted than it started, and a short greedy one gains almost nothing.

game_hooks: PATRON (compounding-wealth build) + BOSS. Bune is the long-game money patron: stipend-based boons that compound across a run and a growing escort of dead retainers, directly from 'He giveth Riches unto a Man' plus 'causeth the Spirits which be under him to gather together upon your Sepulchres'. BOSS SKETCH (discoverable win condition, per the architecture rule): the three-headed dragon is unkillable while his legions hold consecrated graves around the arena — each head is anchored to one occupied sepulchre, and the fight is won by clearing or re-consecrating the graves in the right order, not by damage. ARC HOOK (rot/graves/dragons): he is the range's dragon-plus-necropolis entry and the natural landlord of any plague-pit content — 'he changeth the Place of the Dead' is a licence to move an entire cemetery, and an entire infection, wherever the story needs it. Contrast with Foras, who keeps people alive: Bune profits either way.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1 (contemporary demonolatry works his name heavily as a money spirit, but that is fringe revival practice, not adherence). Known inside occult and demon-collecting circles, thin mainstream carriage = recognition 2 -> rare. Influence 1 -> normal tier. depiction_risk low — the closest call in the low band, since Bune is arguably the most-invoked goetic name in current online demonolatry; still revival-scale, so low, not living.

epithets_traditional: Giver of Tongues and Good Servants

symbols: a beautifully tailored suit with nothing agreed inside it
a staffing roster of loyal servants
a phrasebook for every faction on the floor
a favour called in from an enemy
animals: no fixed beast — the grimoire says only 'a Monster'

temperament: The register declines to say what Ronove looks like — 'a Monster' is the whole description — and he has leaned into it, turning up in excellent tailoring to explain, in your own language and three you did not know you needed, why everyone in this room including your enemies would rather do you a favour.

favor_conditions: recruit an NPC or defector into your crew and finish the floor with them alive
convert a hostile encounter into a standing favour — turn a foe into a contact
translate an untranslated inscription, sign, or enemy transmission before engaging
taboos: sacrifice one of your own servants to save yourself
open a negotiation you have no intention of concluding
patron_block.blessing_style: retinue and tongue — boons are staff and language rather than force: extra hands who fight for free, every faction on the floor made negotiable, and enemy communications rendered legible. A Ronove party gets bigger and better informed each floor instead of stronger.

game_hooks: PATRON (retinue/diplomacy build) + the casino's agent-and-interpreter desk. Straight from the grimoire: he 'giveth Good Servants, Knowledge of Tongues, and Favours with Friends or Foes' — so his boons are a growing free-companion roster, universal comprehension of enemy speech and signage, and a favour-token economy that turns defeated factions into future support. This is the party-size patron: it scales headcount, not stats, which changes encounter maths without touching damage numbers. His undefined form is a genuine asset — the studio's costume department can never agree what to put on camera, so he appears as a differently-shaped monster in every appearance and the show treats it as a running continuity error. Fits the rhetoric triad with Naberius (restores standing) and Forneus (wins the crowd).
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Carried above pure specialist tier mainly by a prominent role in Umineko When They Cry plus occult circulation = recognition 2 -> rare. Influence 1 -> normal tier. depiction_risk low.

epithets_traditional: the Mighty, Great and Terrible Duke

symbols: a crown of gold worn over cavalry red
a summoning ring that must be on the finger
base metal going into an assay furnace and coming out currency

temperament: A Duke in red on a red horse with a gold crown, who speaks in a very clear and subtle voice and will turn anything you hand him into money. The register is specific that you must be wearing the ring when you call him — the house has learned not to ask what he is like when you are not.

favor_conditions: transmute junk loot into house currency at a terminal instead of discarding it
open and close an encounter in a single decisive engagement — one charge, no attrition
honour a sealed contract to the letter for its full term while wearing his ring
taboos: break or renegotiate a sealed contract mid-term
scrap or flat-sell a unique item rather than transmuting it
patron_block.blessing_style: transmutation and warrant — worthless loot becomes currency at a fixed rate, and paper promotions become enforceable rank. Both effects are conditional on the ring: unequip it and the exchange rate and the warrants stop being reliable in ways he is not obliged to warn you about.

game_hooks: DEALER (the house cashier) + PATRON with a hard equipment gate. Two grimoire facts do the work: 'He can turn all metals into Gold' is the vendor loop — a junk-to-currency converter that makes trash loot a build resource — and 'Thou must make use of a Ring in calling him forth' is the constraint: his conversion rate and his granted ranks only hold while the player has his signet equipped, so taking Berith costs a permanent accessory slot for the whole run. That is a clean, legible trade and it hangs directly off the Solomonic ring apparatus already in the corpus (see abrahamic_folk_seal_of_solomon). 'He can give Dignities, and can confirm them unto Man' gives him the promotions desk: he is who a contestant petitions to have a battlefield rank made official on the show's ladder. Later demonological tradition made him a notorious liar who answers falsely unless the ring compels him — keep the ring as the honesty mechanism and the ambiguity as flavour.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1 (the name descends from the Canaanite covenant god Ba'al Berith of Judges 8:33 — a demonized extinct deity, which does not restore worship weight to the goetic Duke). Encyclopedia and game-bestiary tier = recognition 2 -> rare. Influence 1 -> normal tier. depiction_risk low; considered raising it on the demonized-Canaanite-deity ancestry, held at low because the entity depicted here is the grimoire Duke, not Ba'al Berith.

Judges 8:33, 9:4 (PD) — Baal-berith, the demonized covenant god behind the name

epithets_traditional: He Who Tells How the Spirits Fell

symbols: a viper carried in the right hand
a saddle on an infernal dragon-beast
a magical ring held up at face height, defensively
an open confessional file on the fall of the angels

temperament: A Mighty Duke in the shape of a hurtful angel, riding a dragon with a viper in his fist, whose professional hazard is his own breath — you are advised to keep a ring between your face and his. He will tell you anything: every secret, every prophecy, and at length and unprompted the full story of how the spirits fell and precisely why he did.

favor_conditions: win an encounter in which a lingering airborne, poison, or infection condition lands the kill
extract a secret from a boss before killing it — complete an interrogation objective
hold position inside a hazard cloud for a full round without leaving it
taboos: cleanse or vent the field's miasma
kill an informant before it has finished talking
patron_block.blessing_style: exhalation and disclosure — you carry a poison aura that is also an interrogation tool: everything that dies inside your cloud gives up one thing it knew. Boons reward standing in your own filth and letting it work, and pay out in secrets as often as in damage.

game_hooks: TABLE BOSS with an equipment-gated win condition — the cleanest boss in this range. His grimoire danger is not damage output, it is proximity: 'let him not approach too near thee, lest he do thee damage by his Noisome Breath; wherefore the Magician must hold the Magical Ring near his face.' So the fight is a breath-aura DoT that cannot be out-healed or out-damaged, and the discoverable counter is an item (ring/filter/mask) recovered elsewhere on the floor — a proper puzzle-gate, never a damage race, per the architecture rule. As a PATRON he is the miasma build: a persistent poison aura you carry, plus a secret-extraction rider on kills inside it. As a FORSAKEN HOST he is unmatched — he is the only spirit in the register who volunteers the full account of the fall AND the reason for his own, which is the confessional-interview format the broadcast is built on. ARC HOOK (disease/dragons/serpents): the range's strongest plague entry — noxious breath, dragon mount, viper in hand.
rating_notes: No worship of the goetic Duke = influence 1; the name descends from Ashtoreth/Astarte (1 Kings 11:5), a demonized Levantine goddess, and small Semitic-reconstructionist revival worship of ASTARTE exists — that is revival scale and attaches to the goddess, not this Duke. Recognition 4: genuinely a household demon name via Soulcalibur's Astaroth, Ghosts 'n Goblins, Shin Megami Tensei, Darksiders and the Dictionnaire Infernal image (matches Beelzebub/Asmodeus at 4). Influence 1 -> normal tier. depiction_risk: the hardest call in the range — Astaroth is named in living Catholic and evangelical deliverance practice and worked in contemporary demonolatry — but §3.3 reserves 'living' for actively WORSHIPPED figures of major living religions, and being named as an adversary is not worship, so low, consistent with Beelzebub, Asmodeus and Samael. Flagged for owner review.

1 Kings 11:5; Judges 2:13 (PD) — Ashtoreth/Ashtaroth, the demonized goddess behind the name

epithets_traditional: He Who Makes You Beloved of Your Foes

symbols: a favourability poll surfacing from deep water
a good name entered in the register
a phrasebook of every tongue on the floor

temperament: A Marquis who surfaces as a great sea-monster, runs the audience-polling desk, and makes people like you — including, and this is the part he is proud of, the people currently trying to kill you. He considers a good name a more durable asset than a weapon, and the ratings agree with him.

favor_conditions: finish a floor with a net-positive audience approval score, not just a clear
spare a defeated enemy and have that enemy later assist you in the same run
speak with every faction present on a floor before striking any of them
taboos: kill a crowd favourite on camera
refuse a surrender
patron_block.blessing_style: goodwill — approval is the currency and it converts directly to materiel: high audience favour buys supply drops, safe passage and defections, and enemies you beat without humiliating come back as allies. Boons scale with the ratings meter, so under Forneus the show's opinion is a stat.

game_hooks: PATRON (audience/approval build) — the patron that welds the combat layer to the broadcast layer. 'He causeth men to have a good Name' and 'maketh one to be beloved of his Foes as well as of his Friends' become one system: an approval meter that Forneus lets you spend, buying supply drops, safe passage and mid-run enemy defections. That gives non-lethal and theatrical play a real mechanical payoff in a dungeon crawler that otherwise pays only for kills, and it is the cleanest patron-side expression of the reality-show frame in the range. DEALER role: he runs the polling desk, so he is also the diegetic source of the ratings UI. His 29 legions are 'partly of the Order of Thrones and partly of that of Angels' — pair him with Purson (Virtues and Thrones) as the two Throne-staffed houses, which gives a ready-made mid-game bureaucratic rivalry.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. A specialist name even by goetic standards, minimal media carriage = recognition 1 -> mythic. Influence 1 -> normal tier. depiction_risk low.

Weyer, Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (1577) §Forneus (PD) — sea-monster form, rhetoric, good name, tongues, beloved of foes, 29 legions of Thrones and Angels

symbols: a herbal and a lapidary open side by side
an actuarial table of remaining years
a lost-property claim honoured in full
a syllabus of logic and ethics
animals: no beast — he appears simply as a strong man

temperament: The only spirit in this stretch of the register who bothers to look like an ordinary strong man, and the only one selling more time. He teaches logic and ethics with a straight face, tells you exactly what every herb and stone in your bag does, finds what you dropped, and quietly extends your life — which in this building is the rarest product on the floor.

favor_conditions: recover a lost item — retrieve dropped gear or return a stolen relic to its owner
clear a lethal-tier floor without any contestant dropping below a set health threshold
correctly identify an affliction and counter it with the right reagent rather than raw healing
taboos: abandon a downed ally's gear on the field
take a shortcut that trades lifespan, durability, or a timer for speed
patron_block.blessing_style: longevity — his boons extend rather than amplify. Timers run longer, conditions decay slower, durations stretch, revives return, and losses are recoverable. Nothing he grants raises a damage number; the entire package is that you are still here, still equipped, on floor twelve.

game_hooks: PATRON (attrition/survival spine) — the single most arc-load-bearing spirit in this range. The grimoire gives him four powers that assemble into one coherent build: 'know the Virtues of all Herbs and Precious Stones' (reagent-based cures that counter specific afflictions rather than generic healing), 'maketh men... to Live Long' (extended timers, slowed condition decay, extra revives), 'maketh men Invisible' (a disengage, not an assassination tool — escape, in keeping with the rest of his kit), and 'can discover Treasures and recover things Lost' (a corpse-run mechanic: retrieve the gear you died holding). ARC HOOK (plague/rot/immortality/healing): Foras is the designated anti-decay patron — every rot, infection and countdown mechanic the arc introduces has its counterplay routed through him, and he is the explicit counterpart to Bune, who monetises the dead either way. Materia-medica triad with Marax (names the reagent) and Stolas (reads which one the sky calls for). Textual note: Marax's variant name Foraii collides with Foras/Forcas in the manuscripts — play the two as feuding near-namesakes over the same herbarium.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Specialist-only; carries essentially no popular presence = recognition 1 -> mythic. Influence 1 -> normal tier. depiction_risk low. Obscurity is not weakness here: per §3.2 a mythic-tier patron is rare on the boards, which makes drawing the longevity desk a genuine collector's event.
