epithets_traditional: the Great President and Mighty Prince
He Who Carries and Re-Carries Men

symbols: four kings walking behind one guide
a southern-sign almanac with the window circled
a familiar prised out of a rival's custody
a transit manifest with no travel time on it
animals: no fixed beast — he appears in human shape

temperament: A President who is also a Prince and works as neither: he walks ahead of four great kings showing them where their tables are, and in the same shift moves contestants across the venue faster than the schedule permits, poaches other houses' familiars out of custody, and — his other listed office — makes people ignorant, which the floor management finds extremely useful.

favor_conditions: reach a floor's exit inside a hard time limit
take a rival patron's familiar or summon off the board and finish the floor commanding it
escort an NPC across a hostile zone without losing them
taboos: end a floor with the clock nearly expired — lingering is the insult
abandon an escort mid-transit
patron_block.blessing_style: conveyance — boons are movement and displacement rather than force: blink-steps, extra actions, party-wide repositioning, and the standing right to remove another patron's servant from the board and put it on yours. Under Gaap you do not win the fight, you finish the floor before it happens.

game_hooks: PATRON (mobility/speedrun build) with a real availability gate, plus the house's transit chief. Three grimoire facts become three mechanics. (1) 'He can carry and re-carry men very speedily from one Kingdom to another' = the movement kit: blink-steps, party teleports, extra actions — the speedrun/escort patron. (2) 'He can deliver Familiars out of the custody of other Magicians' = the standout hook, a PVP-flavoured steal: take a rival contestant's or rival patron's summon off the board and command it for the rest of the floor. Nothing else in the corpus does this, and it gives the shared-world ladder a natural griefing-with-consent mechanic. (3) 'He appeareth when the Sun is in some of the Southern Signs' = a calendar gate: Gaap is only biddable inside a published in-game seasonal window, which is a clean scarcity lever for the patron-draft economy. His darker listed office — 'to make men insensible or ignorant' — is the debuff side: confusion and knowledge-stripping applied to enemies. Hierarchy: he serves Amaymon, as does Asmodeus ('first and choicest under the power of Amaymon'), making the two grimoire-supported colleagues under an unwritten king — a hook for an off-screen table boss the corpus has not yet had to name.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Specialist-only; negligible pop-culture carriage = recognition 1 -> mythic. Influence 1 -> normal tier. depiction_risk low.

epithets_traditional: the Hart with the Fiery Tail

symbols: a hart whose tail is on fire
a chalked triangle nobody is allowed to scuff
an angel's shape worn only inside the lines
a storm front arriving on cue

temperament: An Earl in the shape of a burning-tailed stag who does not tell the truth — cannot, will not, has never volunteered one — unless he is standing inside a drawn triangle, at which point he becomes an angel with a hoarse voice and answers everything honestly. The house keeps a compliance room chalked on the floor and books him into it.

favor_conditions: win an encounter in which an arena weather or lightning hazard is the killing agent
force a lying NPC into a truth-zone and get the answer out of it
set two bonded enemies against each other — break a pair and let them fight
taboos: act on anything he told you outside the triangle
suppress the weather on a storm floor rather than fighting in it
patron_block.blessing_style: tempest under contract — boons are storms, and their advertised numbers are only reliable while he is inside the binding circle. Take him at his word out on the floor and the buff you are shown is not the buff you have; keep the triangle intact and he is one of the most honest patrons in the register.

game_hooks: PATRON with the range's most distinctive mechanic, taken verbatim from the grimoire: 'He never speaketh truth unless he be compelled, or brought up within a triangle. Being therein, he will take upon himself the form of an Angel.' Implement it as UI honesty — outside a placed triangle, Furfur's boon tooltips display wrong numbers and his forecasts are unreliable; inside one, everything he says is exact and he visibly changes form. The player carries a limited number of placeable triangles per run, so 'when do I spend a truth-zone' becomes a resource decision, and the patron's dishonesty is a systems feature instead of flavour text. Combat kit is weather: 'he raiseth Lightnings and Thunders, Blasts, and great Tempestuous Storms' = arena-wide storm hazards the player can aim. His love office ('he will wittingly urge Love between Man and Woman') is the mirror of Sallos — Sallos bonds pairs, Furfur breaks them for the cameras, which makes the two a natural rival pairing on the broadcast layer. TABLE BOSS: a storm arena where the win condition is to compel him into the triangle at the centre, not to damage the hart.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Modest carriage through demon-collecting games and demonology reference = recognition 2 -> rare. Influence 1 -> normal tier. depiction_risk low.

Weyer, Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (1577) §Furfur (PD) — hart with fiery tail, lies unless within a triangle, then angelic; storms and lightnings; urges love; 26 legions

epithets_traditional: He Who Hopes for the Seventh Throne

symbols: a wolf with griffin's wings and a serpent's tail
fire coming out of a mouth mid-sentence
a service contract with twelve hundred years still to run
an empty seat kept warm on the Seventh Throne

temperament: The register calls him a strong fighter and leaves it there, which is exactly how he would want it. He arrives as a fire-breathing wolf with griffin's wings and a serpent's tail, takes the shape of a man when asked, keeps every term of every contract, and told Solomon to his face that after twelve hundred years he expects to be called back upstairs. Nobody in the building has the heart to check the maths.

favor_conditions: win a boss encounter in straight melee — no hazards, no consumables, no exploit
serve a contract to full term across multiple runs without a single breach
take and hold the front line for an entire floor — finish as the party's highest damage taken
taboos: win by hazard, poison, or exploit when the fight was winnable straight
break a contract early to cash out
patron_block.blessing_style: service — pure combat and nothing else: damage, stance, a breath weapon, and a compounding loyalty stat. His boons grow with cumulative unbroken contract time across runs and reset to nothing on a breach, so Marchosias is the only patron in the register who pays in tenure. Time served is the stat.

game_hooks: PATRON (long-horizon loyalty build) + the range's best CONTESTANT LEGEND. Mechanically he is the tenure patron: an unbroken-contract counter that persists across runs and multiplies his combat boons, wiped entirely by a single breach — a commitment device aimed squarely at players who patron-shop every run, and the natural spine of a meta-progression track. His kit is deliberately unclever: 'He is a strong fighter', plus a fire-breath from 'Vomiting Fire out of his mouth', plus the wolf-to-man shift as a stance toggle (beast form = damage and mobility, man form = precision and party utility). NARRATIVE: he was of the Order of Dominations and told Solomon he hoped after 1,200 years to return to the Seventh Throne — an employee on an impossibly long vesting schedule who has never missed a shift. In the Cosmic Casino frame that is the most sympathetic figure in the goetic range and the obvious contestant-legend: a former executive working the floor, still counting, still expecting the call. Foil to Glasya-Labolas, who is paid for spectacle and has no term to serve.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Carried by demon-collecting games and a steady presence in demonology art and anime bestiaries, short of household tier = recognition 2 -> rare. Influence 1 -> normal tier. depiction_risk low.
sources: The Goetia: The Lesser Key of Solomon the King (Mathers tr., Crowley ed., 1904; public domain) — Ars Goetia, the 72 spirits

Weyer, Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (1577) §Marchosias (PD) — wolf with griffin's wings and serpent's tail, vomits fire, takes man's shape, strong fighter, of the Order of Dominations, hoped to return to the Seventh Throne after 1,200 years, 30 legions

symbols: a star-chart annotated in a raven's hand
a herbarium pressed between lapidary plates
an appraisal slip attached to unidentified loot
an omen window posted on the house board

temperament: A Great and Powerful Prince who arrives as an enormous raven, becomes a man once you have got over it, and then tells you what is actually in your bag. He reads the sky and the pharmacopeia as one document, considers a correctly identified stone worth more than an unidentified sword, and has never been wrong about either.

favor_conditions: identify every unknown item on a floor before you leave it
cure an affliction with the correct herbal counter rather than brute healing
complete a run inside a named celestial window the house has posted
taboos: use, sell, or equip an unidentified stone or reagent
ignore a posted omen or timing window
patron_block.blessing_style: reading — boons are information made actionable: full item identification, exact condition tooltips, a forecast of the next floor's hazard, and the reagent knowledge to counter it in advance. He never raises a number; he removes every unknown from the screen, which in a lethal crawler is the same thing.

game_hooks: PATRON (information/appraisal build) + the house's appraisal desk. His two grimoire offices — 'He teacheth the Art of Astronomy, and the Virtues of Herbs and Precious Stones' — become one system: astronomy is the forecast (the next floor's hazard and the timing windows the house publishes), herbs-and-stones is the appraisal (full identification of drops and exact affliction tooltips). That makes him the natural first patron for new contestants and the diagnostician of the materia-medica triad: STOLAS names the disease and reads which reagent the sky calls for, MARAX names what the reagent does, FORAS makes the cure hold. ARC HOOK (plague/healing): the diagnosis half of the cure loop — without a Stolas read, an affliction shows as an unnamed debuff and the player is guessing. RECOGNITION NOTE: he is the one goetic spirit in this range with genuine current mainstream pull thanks to Helluva Boss, so he is the obvious marquee draw for a goetic patron banner — but keep the corpus portrayal grimoire-first (raven, astronomy, herbs), not derivative of any modern property.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1. Recognition 4: unusually high for a goetic spirit and earned by current mainstream carriage — Stolas is a lead character in Helluva Boss, which has put the name well beyond occult circles, plus Shin Megami Tensei and long-standing demonology art (matches Beelzebub, Asmodeus, Astaroth at 4; not 5, which is reserved for global household names). Influence 1 -> normal tier per §3.5 — high recognition does not buy table tier. depiction_risk low; the modern-media association is an IP-adjacency note, not a sensitivity one, and ip_status stays traditional because we take the figure from the 1904 public-domain grimoire, not from any modern depiction.
sources: The Goetia: The Lesser Key of Solomon the King (Mathers tr., Crowley ed., 1904; public domain) — Ars Goetia, the 72 spirits
Weyer, Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (1577) §Stolas (PD) — raven form, then a man; astronomy, virtues of herbs and precious stones; 26 legions

temperament: The lounge act the floor cannot stop booking: sings in a child's voice until somebody has the presence of mind to order him into a man's shape, and only then starts answering questions — marvellously, on every science there is. The most obedient thing in the building, and only because he is 1,200 years into a parole hearing for the Seventh Throne.

favor_conditions: close an encounter on a Camera Call flourish instead of a killing blow — win the crowd, not just the fight
clear a lore or riddle gate with the answer you were taught rather than forcing it open
obey a table ruling you disagree with, in full, for an entire floor
taboos: cut a performance short — skip a broadcast beat to rush a kill
destroy a codex, score, or lore pickup instead of reading it
patron_block.blessing_style: encore — boons are rebirths: one death per run rewritten as a costume change, priced entirely in how well the audience was performing for. He is a Marquis of 20 legions and gives knowledge freely; he will not give power, only another verse.

game_hooks: Patron: signature boon is a once-per-run self-resurrection that only arms if the run's Camera Call/audience meter cleared a threshold — the phoenix is literally paid for by the broadcast. Dealer at the lounge table (a non-combat knowledge node: he answers any one question about the next floor, correctly). Boss sketch (silence-the-song): while Phenex is singing, every enemy in the arena is buff-locked and damage against him is halved; the discoverable win condition is the grimoire's own instruction — do not listen to the song, command him into human shape (an interact, not an attack), which strips the aura. Conditions burn / madness_dream.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only figure with no worship = influence 1; carried into pop culture by anime and game demon rosters (and buoyed by the phoenix association the name trades on) = recognition 2 — the upper end of the obscure goetic pack.

temperament: A hoarse grey dove who builds the tower, fills it with weapons and ammunition, and posts the men-of-war wherever the table tells him to — and has never once asked which side he is stocking. Twenty-six legions of pure logistics: the only Earl on the floor whose entire office is making sure the violence has somewhere to happen.

favor_conditions: fortify a position and hold it through a full siege wave without giving ground
enter a boss arena at full ammunition and consumables — spend nothing on the approach
resupply an ally mid-run: hand over a weapon or ammunition you could have kept
taboos: abandon a fortified position you built or were given
walk into a named arena under-equipped — empty ammunition, no consumables
patron_block.blessing_style: materiel — boons arrive as stock, never as strength: ammunition, armour, and a prepared position delivered before the fight starts and never once during it. Whatever you did not carry in, he will not conjure for you.

game_hooks: Patron: a pre-run loadout economy — Halphas's boons are all issued at the arena door (extra magazines, an armour tier, a pre-placed barricade), which makes him the counter-patron to improvisational builds and the perfect fit for the sheet's `magazine` item field. Table boss over a fortress/tower floor: a defence encounter where waves are dispatched to fixed points ('sendeth men-of-war to places appointed') and the discoverable win condition is to cut the supply line into the tower rather than clear the waves. Conditions crushed / burn.
rating_notes: Pure grimoire construct, no cult, no practice footprint = influence 1; essentially unknown outside demonology lists and the occasional metal album = recognition 1.

temperament: Lands as a crow, takes a man's shape when asked, and tells you in a hoarse voice exactly what your enemies want, think, and have already done — the best intelligence desk in the building. He accepts every offering kindly and willingly, and cheats every single person who makes one.

favor_conditions: scout an arena to full reveal before engaging anything in it
bind a familiar or summon and finish the floor with it still alive
win an encounter by countering a telegraphed action you knew was coming
taboos: open on an unscouted room — attack before the arena is revealed
spend a familiar's life for a short-term gain
patron_block.blessing_style: intelligence, adulterated — boons are enemy intent handed to you in advance, plus artificers and good familiars gathered from anywhere on the board; and because he receives every sacrifice willingly and deceives whoever makes it, roughly one detail in ten is quietly, deliberately wrong.

game_hooks: The dataset's cleanest 'unreliable oracle' mechanic, straight from the text: any offering made to Malphas returns a real, valuable, and subtly corrupted boon — enemy intent, hidden-room maps, boss timers — with one salted entry the player has to catch. fidelity 1. Also the summoner/builder patron: 'bringeth artificers together from all places' = a crafting-bench boon that pools materials across the party, and 'giveth good familiars' = a persistent summon. Boss sketch: a tower he is still building, which grows a floor every time you accept one of his gifts — the discoverable win condition is to refuse the offerings and climb a short tower.
rating_notes: No worship, grimoire-only = influence 1; one of the more-borrowed goetic names in games and demon-lore fiction, and a fixture in modern pathworking lists = recognition 2.

symbols: a king's strongbox in a crow's claws

temperament: A demoted Throne working the floor as its best fence: lifts treasure out of a king's own house, carries it wherever you name, and can tell you what happened, what is happening, and what will — all in the same breath. If he cannot steal your standing he will simply level the city it sits in, then talk your two worst enemies into liking each other on the way out.

favor_conditions: take a boss's reward by theft — clear a vault or heist objective without triggering the fight
raze a named structure objective to the ground rather than capturing it
end a hostile encounter by turning an enemy into an ally instead of killing it
taboos: leave a hoard or vault un-looted when you could have emptied it
betray an ally you personally reconciled
patron_block.blessing_style: extraction — boons remove rather than empower: he takes the thing instead of beating it. Theft, demolition, and the sudden inexplicable friendliness of somebody who was shooting at you a round ago; all of it delivered somewhere else, because carrying it whither he is commanded is the whole of his office.

game_hooks: Heist-run patron: enables a non-combat clear path (steal the boss's key item out of its arena — in this game, lift the phylactery/win-condition object itself and skip the damage race entirely, which is exactly the design the architecture doc wants). 'Destroy cities and dignities of men' = an arena-demolition verb and a reputation-attack against rival contestants on the leaderboard. 'Cause love between friends and foes' = the pacify/recruit mechanic. Messenger role covers the courier half: he delivers stolen goods to a named drop, which is a natural async-show (Stage 2) contract.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no practice or worship = influence 1; a specialist name, effectively unknown to a general audience despite occasional game cameos = recognition 1.

symbols: a warship going down by the bow
gryphon wings on a man's back

temperament: A winged Duke with power over both winds and seas who will sink every hull on the board — and will not touch a single one if somebody remembers to say so out loud. He is 1,000 years into a hope of returning to the Seventh Throne, and the only thing he still respects is a limit that was stated clearly.

favor_conditions: win a flooded or storm-flagged arena without leaving the water
declare an enemy spared at the start of an encounter and honour it to the end
sink an enemy vessel or vehicle objective instead of boarding and clearing it
taboos: kill an enemy you had already declared spared
drain, freeze, or otherwise remove the water from an arena
patron_block.blessing_style: restraint under power — boons are enormous and conditional: storm, wind, and drowning force that stay yours exactly as long as you keep the limits you named out loud. He will not hurt any man or thing if commanded to the contrary, and expects the same discipline back.

game_hooks: Boss sketch (declared-restraint): the arena floods on a fixed schedule and no damage output can outpace it; the discoverable win condition is to issue the binding command — an interact that names a restraint Focalor is grimoire-bound to keep — after which he holds the water off for as long as the party keeps its own declared limit. Breaks the moment the party breaks its word. Conditions suffocation / chilled. As patron he is the game's cleanest 'oath economy': the more limits you announce on camera, the bigger the boon, and the harsher the loss when you break one.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no living practice = influence 1; specialist recognition only — the drowning-duke sea demon rarely surfaces in mainstream media = recognition 1. Mathers gives 30 legions; Weyer's earlier Pseudomonarchia reads 'three legions' — the Mathers figure is used here.

symbols: a mermaid at the helm of a munitions convoy
a phantom fleet on the horizon
a wound with a three-day clock

temperament: Guides your convoy of arms and armour safely into port with one hand and opens a three-day wound in you with the other; the storm is real, the fleet on the horizon is mostly not, and the worms breeding in the cut are extremely real. Twenty-nine legions of patient maritime rot who has never seen the point of killing anything today.

favor_conditions: let an infected or poison condition run its full duration and land the killing tick — never burst the target down
escort a supply or cargo objective across a water arena with the load intact
survive a wave in which the visible enemy count far exceeds the real threat
taboos: cure or cleanse a rot condition you inflicted
scuttle your own convoy to reach a kill faster
patron_block.blessing_style: the three-day wound — boons are delayed-fatal: nothing you strike dies now, it dies on a clock nobody can stop, putrefying on schedule. Safe passage for whatever you are carrying comes free; the illusion of a fleet that is not there comes free too.

game_hooks: ARC-CRITICAL plague vector. Patron mechanic: Vepar's mark converts any wound into an unremovable 3-turn death timer — damage that cannot be healed, cleansed, or outraced, only outlived, which is the purest expression of the sim's no-to-hit-roll design (it just happens). Boss sketch (phantom fleet): the arena fills with ships and most of them are illusions; the discoverable win condition is to identify the one real hull rather than clear the wave, and every illusion attacked costs a turn on your own rot clock. Conditions infected / poison / suffocation.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no worship = influence 1; a boss cameo here and there (Bloodstained) but no general-audience presence = recognition 1.

temperament: An armed soldier with a lion's head on a pale-coloured horse who builds you high towers, castles and cities and furnishes them with armour — then afflicts men for many days with wounds and with sores rotten and full of worms. Fifty legions, the largest command in this stretch of the book, and his actual weapon is the calendar.

favor_conditions: hold a fortified arena through a full siege without losing a wall segment
kill a boss on accumulated rot — let infection or poison land the final tick, not a burst
finish a floor with every party member's armour unbroken
taboos: cleanse an infection, on yourself or an enemy, before it has run its full course
abandon a wall or gate you were tasked to hold
patron_block.blessing_style: siegecraft and gangrene — boons come in two halves that only make sense together: fortification and armour that outlast the fight, and a wound on your weapon that keeps working for many days after the fight ends. He gives good familiars to anyone patient enough to still be there.

game_hooks: ARC-CRITICAL: the plague-siege boss and the single best rot anchor in the range — 'afflicteth men for many days with wounds and with sores rotten and full of worms' is a literal multi-encounter DOT that persists ACROSS floors, not within one fight. Boss sketch: inside his own walls Sabnock cannot be out-damaged (armour and reinforcement scale with time); the discoverable win condition is to demolish the tower he built rather than fight the soldier on it — structural collapse, not DPS. As patron he is the attrition build's home: everything he grants pays out late. Conditions infected / bleeding / crushed. Pale horse + rot makes him the natural pestilence-rider silhouette without importing the Revelation figure directly.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no worship = influence 1; unusually visible for a mid-list goetic name thanks to a headline anime demon character built on him, plus steady presence in protection-magic pathworking = recognition 2.

temperament: Takes away the sight, the hearing, or the understanding of anyone at the table on request, steals money straight out of a king's house, and promises to bring it back in 1,200 years. Fetch him horses, fetch him anything — but pen him in a triangle first, because outside one he will deceive you and tell you many lies with a hoarse, extremely reasonable voice.

favor_conditions: blind, deafen, or confuse a boss before it completes a telegraphed action
clear a guarded vault and leave the floor without ever being seen
pin the terms of an offer before accepting it — take a boon only with its stated limit declared
taboos: accept an unbounded offer — take a boon without first fixing its terms
return stolen loot to its owner
patron_block.blessing_style: sensory theft on credit — boons strip an enemy's sight, hearing, and understanding, and fetch you whatever you name; the price is a loan repayable in 1,200 years, which is to say never, and every unbound promise arrives with a lie folded into it.

game_hooks: The triangle is the mechanic. Every Shax boon is offered in two forms: BOUND (spend an action constraining the terms — the boon does exactly what it says) or UNBOUND (free and immediate — one stated effect in three is a lie, rolled from the command stream, so it is deterministic and replayable). That gives the sim a real risk/tempo decision with no hidden randomness. Debuff patron: blind/deafen/stun applied to boss telegraphs. As a dealer he runs the house's loan window — borrow now, repay in 1,200 years — which is how a contestant gets over-leveraged before a VIP table. Conditions madness_dream-adjacent (understanding removed) / exhausted.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no worship = influence 1; the name has real reach through a best-selling YA franchise's 'Shax demons' and the Netflix adaptation, well above the goetic mid-list = recognition 2.

epithets_traditional: the Lion on the Black Horse

symbols: a viper held like a pen
a tower and its rubble side by side

temperament: Sits down holding two ranks at once — King and Earl — on a black horse, with a viper in his hand like a pen, and reads the table's hidden cards out loud: what is concealed, who is a witch, what has happened and what is coming. Then he decides whether the walls stay up, because he builds towers and overthrows great stone walls with the same shrug.

favor_conditions: expose a hidden enemy, trap, or concealed room before it triggers
kill a concealed caster or witch-tagged enemy that was hiding among ordinary mobs
open a boss arena by destroying its wall rather than using its gate
taboos: leave a concealed enemy unexposed at the end of an encounter
play a hidden hand — conceal your own build or loadout from the broadcast
patron_block.blessing_style: exposure — boons are revelation with teeth: hidden things named aloud, witches and wizards picked out of a crowd, and the stone wall that was hiding them pulled down by storm. Whatever was behind it gets the viper.

game_hooks: ARC-RELEVANT (serpent): the viper is the range's cleanest snake motif and the natural dissolution/poison applicator. The anti-stealth patron — his boon permanently reveals concealed enemies, traps, and the identity of a hidden 'witch' unit, which makes him the direct counter to Shax and Balam builds and a perfect fit for the show's traitor/expose format. Boss sketch (demolition): a walled maze arena where the lion is unkillable in the open; the discoverable win condition is to use his own storm to bring the walls down on him — build and overthrow are the same office, so the arena is the weapon. Dual rank (King AND Earl) justifies a two-phase fight with two different rule sets. Conditions poison / dissolution / crushed.
rating_notes: Rated influence 2, not 1: Vine is one of the few spirits in this range with a genuine present-day devotional footprint — a regularly-worked, named patron in contemporary demonolatry and left-hand-path pathworking, comparable in scale to the small organised Lilith veneration already recorded at influence 2. Recognition 2: the name appears across game demon rosters and modern occult publishing, but 'Vine' is generic enough that no general audience attaches it to a goetic king. Depiction risk raised to `living` for the same reason — see rating on influence; also the 'discovereth Witches' line carries real witch-hunt freight and should be played as exposure-of-the-concealed, never as persecution.

symbols: a star chart and a set-square
a lapidary's tray of stones and cut woods

temperament: The smallest command in the whole stretch — six legions — and by some distance the tidiest hands: arrives as a monster, becomes a man when told, and quietly moves the dead somewhere better without being asked. Then he lights candles that only seem to be candles over the graves he emptied, so nobody thinks to check.

favor_conditions: recover a fallen ally's body and carry it to a safe extraction point
identify a material's true properties before using it — appraise the stone or wood instead of guessing
solve an astrology or geometry gate on its own terms rather than brute-forcing it
taboos: leave a body where it fell when you could have carried it
destroy a corpse or break open a grave for loot
patron_block.blessing_style: quiet relocation — boons move things rather than strengthen them: bodies out of the kill zone, materials correctly named before you waste them, and a false light left behind so that whatever was following you stops at the wrong grave.

game_hooks: Three separable systems, all literal readings of the text. (1) 'Changeth dead bodies and putteth them in another place' = corpse recovery / revive-at-a-distance: a downed ally can be relocated to a safe node instead of resurrected in place. (2) 'Teacheth the virtues of precious stones and woods' = the crafting appraisal bench, which is exactly what the live campaign's material bands need (identify before you spend). (3) 'Lighteth seeming candles upon the graves of the dead' = a decoy mechanic — false objective markers that pull enemy aggro to empty graves; note the grimoire's own word is SEEMING, the lights are an appearance, not fire. Boss sketch: a cemetery arena lit with dozens of candles, only one of which stands over an occupied grave; win condition is finding the real one, not clearing the field.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no worship = influence 1; a specialist name known almost entirely to demonology readers and necromantic pathworkers = recognition 1. Legion count is textually unstable: Mathers reads 6, Weyer reads 26, some later printings 60 — the Mathers figure (6) is used, and the smallness is deliberately made characterful rather than papered over.

symbols: a dromedary crossing an empty floor

temperament: A Power of the old order reduced to a mighty dromedary with a bad accent — speaks the Egyptian tongue, but not perfectly, and never has. Still crosses any distance without stopping, still procures the love of women and friendship between friends and foes, and still tells you what was, what is, and what will be; half the words come out wrong and all of it works anyway.

favor_conditions: cross a full floor without a rest or resupply stop
turn a hostile faction or NPC into an ally through dialogue instead of combat
clear a translation or inscription gate using the partial text you actually have
taboos: kill an NPC you have already made friendly
leave a companion behind in hostile terrain
patron_block.blessing_style: the long haul — boons are endurance and reconciliation: stamina enough to cross anything without stopping, and standing enough to make an enemy shake your hand. The wording always comes out slightly wrong; it has never once mattered.

game_hooks: Traversal/endurance patron for long desert or wasteland floors — his boon removes the resupply stop entirely (dromedary logic: you carry the fight in with you). Diplomacy hook: one hostile group per floor can be converted through dialogue rather than combat, which is the cheapest way to give the tactical layer a non-combat clear. The 'Egyptian tongue, but not perfectly' line is a gift for a puzzle system — translation gates that deliberately return a partial, slightly-wrong reading, and the correct play is to act on it anyway rather than hunt for a clean one. Order of Potestates backstory pairs him with Crocell for a two-hander of fallen Powers working the floor.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no worship = influence 1; a low-visibility name even among demon-lore audiences — the camel form is his only memorable hook = recognition 1.

symbols: a crucible of base metal running gold
two identical glasses, one wine one water

temperament: A mighty winged bull who makes men wise and instructs them in divers things, transmutes all metals into gold, and turns wine into water and water into wine — the floor's alchemist and its most useful bartender in one. The most generous thing in the range, and the only one who will sober you up at exactly the moment you did not want him to.

favor_conditions: convert junk loot into currency or upgrade material rather than discarding it — bank every drop
clear an encounter completely sober: no consumable buffs active at any point
spend a full floor's takings on a single skill upgrade instead of gear
taboos: vendor-trash a unique material
walk into a boss fight stacked on consumables
patron_block.blessing_style: transmutation — boons convert instead of adding: any resource becomes any other at his table, including the one you needed and could not buy. Metal into gold, wine into water, water back into wine; nothing is created, everything is exchanged, and he takes no cut.

game_hooks: The economy patron. Signature system: a universal converter bench — any resource class exchanges for any other at a posted rate (metals to gold, consumables to materials, and the wine/water pair as a literal buff/debuff toggle). That is a direct answer to the live campaign's loot-band problem, where players hold materials they cannot use. His 'sober' favour condition makes him the deliberate counter-patron to consumable-stacking builds: take his boons and the pre-fight buffet is closed. Investor role fits the transmutation angle — he is the one goetic spirit who can actually manufacture the bankroll rather than steal it. Boss sketch: an arena where every pickup silently transmutes into something else on a fixed cycle, and the win condition is to time the cycle rather than fight the bull.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no worship = influence 1; near-invisible outside demonology lists, though the alchemy hook gets him occasional game cameos = recognition 1.

symbols: an angel's face on a duke's shoulders
steam rising off a found spring
the roar of a flood in a dry room

temperament: Still wears the angel face he had as a Power, still speaks mystically of hidden things, and still knows where every warm water in the building runs — he finds baths where there was no water and heats them for nothing. He also fills rooms with the roaring of great waters that are not there, which is exactly why nobody quite trusts the free bath.

favor_conditions: extract to a spring or rest node with the entire party alive
break contact with a wave using the roar as misdirection instead of fighting it
clear a geometry or architecture gate to open a hidden route
taboos: start a fight inside a designated rest or healing node
wall off or destroy a water source another party could have used
patron_block.blessing_style: the warm room — boons are restoration and misdirection in one gift: hidden hot springs found where the map said there was no water, and the roaring of many waters covering your retreat from a flood that does not exist.

game_hooks: ARC-CRITICAL: the healer of the range and the only genuine cure-side patron in it — 'warmeth Waters, and discovereth Baths' is a literal mid-floor healing node, and it is the natural counterweight to Vepar's and Sabnock's rot. Mechanic: Crocell's boon reveals a hidden thermal spring somewhere on the current floor which clears chilled / exhausted / bleeding and partially arrests infection — the party has to reach it, so it is a routing decision, not a button. Second mechanic straight from the text: 'great Noises and Roarings of Waters, although there be none' = a phantom-flood disengage that pulls enemy pathing toward a flood that is not happening. Boss sketch: an arena drowned in the sound of water with no water in it — the discoverable win condition is to ignore the roar entirely and act on the real map, because every reaction to the sound is what actually kills you. His angelic form makes him the range's best 'morally alien, not evil' showcase: he heals for free and it is still unsettling.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no worship = influence 1; a specialists-only name despite one of the most distinctive offices in the book = recognition 1. The Potestates/Powers backstory is stated in the text itself (declared unto King Solomon) and is load-bearing for the angel-faced presentation.

epithets_traditional: the Only Knight of the Seventy-Two

symbols: a pitchfork carried like a lecturer's pointer

temperament: The lowest rank in the entire book — the only Knight among seventy-two kings and dukes — and by a distance the sharpest tongue on the floor: a cruel old man with a hoary head on a pale horse, holding a sharp weapon he mostly uses to point at your mistakes. Teaches philosophy, astrology, rhetoric, logic, palmistry and pyromancy in all their parts and perfectly, and has outlived everyone who ever argued with him.

favor_conditions: execute the exact sequence a divination or foreshadowing beat showed you
beat a boss on the first attempt after learning its complete tell set
win a dispute or negotiation gate on the correct chain of argument
taboos: brute-force a puzzle after being shown the answer
dismiss an omen or foreshadowing beat without reading it
patron_block.blessing_style: the hard curriculum — boons are foreknowledge you have to earn: exact tells, exact timings, fire and palm read in advance, all of it perfect and none of it free. He gives nothing whatsoever to anyone who will not sit through the lesson first.

game_hooks: ARC-RELEVANT (longevity): the range's age-and-endurance figure — a hoary old man on a pale-coloured horse who wins by outlasting, and whose entire kit is knowledge that only pays off on a second encounter. Mechanic: Furcas's boon permanently reveals enemy tells and windup timings, but ONLY for enemy types you have already survived once — the lesson has to be attended. That turns the sim's deterministic command-stream replay into a progression system rather than a save-scum. Boss sketch: an old knight who counters whatever line you played last time (he reads the command log the way he reads a palm), so the discoverable win condition is to never repeat a sequence — the one boss in the range you cannot solve by learning a rotation. Pyromancy gives him burn; the pitchfork gives him bleeding. Being the sole Knight makes him a natural low-tier patron who punches far above his table.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no worship = influence 1; recognised chiefly for the trivia that he is the only Knight of the seventy-two, not for himself = recognition 1.

symbols: a goshawk on a gauntleted fist

temperament: Three heads — bull, man and ram — one hoarse voice, a serpent's tail, flaming eyes, a furious bear underneath him and a goshawk on his fist: the most over-specified silhouette in the book, arriving at your table to answer perfectly on things past, present and to come. He tells the truth about your future because it is funnier than lying, then makes you invisible so you have to watch it happen without being able to warn anybody.

favor_conditions: clear an entire arena undetected — complete the encounter without ever entering combat
win a fight in which a beast pack outnumbered you
call your own outcome before an encounter and hit it exactly
taboos: kill a bird- or beast-tagged companion
break stealth to take a kill you had already secured another way
patron_block.blessing_style: invisibility and the straight answer — boons are unseen positioning plus a true, unwelcome forecast of what is coming. His three heads never agree on how to phrase it and have never once disagreed on the facts.

game_hooks: ARC-RELEVANT (serpent): the tail is a real serpent, not a decoration — poison/dissolution applicator on an otherwise beast-and-stealth kit. The stealth patron: full invisibility plus a truthful pre-fight forecast, and 'to be witty' reads cleanly as a dialogue/dispute bonus. Boss sketch (three-phase, one body): each head runs its own phase with its own rule set, and killing them out of order re-enrages the others — the discoverable win condition is to kill the FURIOUS BEAR he rides rather than the king on it, dismounting a King who cannot fight on foot. The goshawk is a separate summoned harasser that must be dealt with first or it keeps re-spotting the party. Shares Asmodeus's exact bull/man/ram + serpent-tail iconography, which is a real grimoire correspondence and a free lore link to an entity already in the roster. Conditions poison / dissolution / crushed.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no worship = influence 1; boosted to recognition 2 by heavy game and demon-roster use and by name-collision with the biblical Balaam, which gets him half-remembered by audiences who have never opened a grimoire.

symbols: a soldier on a great horse
a star chart nailed to a shield

temperament: A soldier on a great horse with a lion's face, very red, with flaming eyes and a hoarse and very big voice — and what he does with all that is teach astronomy and the liberal sciences. Nobody has ever heard him lower his voice, and nobody has ever caught him wrong.

favor_conditions: finish a floor with a granted familiar still alive
win a mounted or charge-based encounter without dismounting
clear a star-chart or navigation gate correctly on the first pass
taboos: spend a granted familiar's life to save your own
break off a charge you had committed to
patron_block.blessing_style: the loud lesson — boons are a good familiar that fights beside you and a star-map that never lies, delivered at a volume that costs you every stealth advantage you were holding.

game_hooks: Summoner patron: a persistent familiar unit that survives between encounters and can be upgraded, plus navigation-gate solving from the astronomy office. Deliberate anti-synergy is the design point — his boons are LOUD ('hoarse and very big' speech), so taking Alloces permanently disables stealth approaches, making him the mechanical opposite of Balam and Shax and forcing a real patron choice rather than a stat comparison. Boss sketch: heavy cavalry on a great horse — raw trades lose, and the discoverable win condition is terrain: break the charge lane, and the Duke who cannot be beaten in a line is beaten by a corner. Conditions crushed / burn (the flaming eyes and red face).
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no worship = influence 1; a low-visibility name with only scattered game appearances — the striking red-lion-cavalry image is far better known than the name attached to it = recognition 1.

symbols: a thrush becoming a man with a sharp sword
coals of fire arranged as an argument

temperament: Arrives as a thrush, becomes a man with a sharp sword, and answers you in burning ashes and coals of fire — the house's best disputer, who has never lost an argument he chose to enter. He gives men the understanding of all birds, the lowing of bullocks, the barking of dogs and the voice of the waters, which means he is the only thing on the floor that hears the whole room.

favor_conditions: win a dispute or judgement encounter by argument rather than violence
avoid an ambush by acting on an animal or environmental warning
read a fire or ash divination beat and act on it before its trigger fires
taboos: kill an animal that gave you a warning
settle a formal dispute by attacking the arbiter
patron_block.blessing_style: translation and testimony — boons turn the arena's noise into information: every bird, bullock, dog and current tells you plainly what is about to happen, and his own answers, written in embers, are true.

game_hooks: The 'listen to the room' patron: with Camio's boon active, ambient fauna and water become a genuine early-warning layer — birds go quiet before an ambush, water changes pitch before a flood trap, and the sim can telegraph without a UI element, which is exactly the kind of diegetic tell the no-to-hit-roll design needs. 'A Good Disputer' plus a sharp sword makes him the natural adjudicating dealer for a non-combat DISPUTE encounter type: a formal argument with a losing condition, refereed by a President who will settle it himself if you cheat. 'Answereth in burning ashes' = an ash-reading divination minigame that costs a burn condition to consult. Order of Angels backstory pairs him with Murmur. Conditions burn / bleeding.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no worship = influence 1; the Caim spelling carries real audience recall from a headline action-RPG protagonist and recurring media use, well above the mid-list = recognition 2.

epithets_traditional: the Crowned Warrior on the Gryphon

symbols: ministers with great trumpets going before him
a shade seated at the interrogation table

temperament: Arrives on a gryphon in a ducal crown with his own ministers blowing great trumpets ahead of him, holding two ranks at once, and then does the single most useful thing in the book: constrains the souls of the dead to come and answer questions. He calls that teaching philosophy perfectly, and he is not entirely wrong.

favor_conditions: interrogate a fallen enemy's or contestant's shade for a boss's win condition before engaging it
recover a dead runner's log or loadout from a previous failed attempt on this floor
announce your entry to a named arena instead of ambushing it — take the fanfare
taboos: silence a shade before it has finished answering
enter a named arena unannounced
patron_block.blessing_style: the summons — boons are testimony from the dead: anyone who died on this floor can be constrained to the table and made to answer, and they arrive on a fanfare that nothing in the building can sleep through.

game_hooks: The strongest shared-world hook in the range and a direct fit for DIRECTION.md's Stage 2 async global show: 'constrain Souls Deceased to come before the Exorcist to answer those questions' is a post-mortem query system — a live run can summon the shade of a PREVIOUS contestant who died on this floor (any run, any player) and interrogate it for the boss's win condition, turning the show's body count into a shared intel layer. Deterministic and command-stream safe: the shade replays logged answers, no wall-clock, no hidden randomness. Cost is the trumpets — every summons is announced, so the whole arena aggros, which makes the mechanic a real decision instead of free information. Boss sketch: the fanfare is mandatory and constant, so nothing in his arena can ever be ambushed; the discoverable win condition is to weaponise the pull — bait the entire floor into one room and use the crowd against the crowned Duke. Conditions exhausted / dissolution.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no worship = influence 1; the demon is far less known than the common word he shares a name with, and rarely surfaces outside demonology lists = recognition 1.

epithets_traditional: the Horse that puts on a Man
he who suffers no other spirit to tempt his client

symbols: a horse's head stamped on a house token
an odds board with nothing hedged

temperament: Comes to the table as a horse and finishes the conversation as a man, and in between tells you exactly what was, what is, and what is coming — no shading, no vig. The one signature on the floor that means what it says: he hands out rank and standing with your friends and your enemies alike, and he does not let another patron near the contestant he is backing.

favor_conditions: run an entire floor under one patron contract — decline every rival patron's counter-offer put in front of you
act on foreknowledge: use a scouted or telegraphed enemy pattern to pre-empt it, instead of reacting after it fires
win a rank or title objective and still hold that standing when the run ends
taboos: break a signed contract or switch patrons mid-run
lie to a table_boss or house arbiter to win a ruling
patron_block.blessing_style: straight answers and safe conduct — boons are unhedged information (enemy patterns, the next hazard, what the floor is actually paying) plus hard immunity to poaching, charm and possession from rival patrons; the only patron whose posted odds are the real odds, and the only one who will not sell your contract out from under you.

game_hooks: The fidelity-5 anchor of the patron roster and the structural answer to Mammon's fidelity-1 buy-out: sign with Orobas and no rival patron can purchase, charm or possess you off his book for the rest of the run — the trade is that you cannot shop around either. Mechanically a pure information patron (reveal telegraphs, name the next hazard, show the true reward table before you commit) plus an anti-poach ward; he adds no damage at all, which is the point. Encounter design: not a boss — a straight dealer whose table is the tutorial for reading the house's real odds, and the NPC who will tell a contestant, flatly and correctly, that they are about to die. Direct foil to Andras (§63), whose office is to kill his own client. contract_fidelity flag.
rating_notes: A grimoire spirit with no living cult and only fringe occult attention = influence 1 (level with Asmodeus / Lucifer / Samael); occult-literate and demon-lore recall plus minor game appearances, well short of household = recognition 2. Held at vip against the influence-1 -> normal default on rank and function: a Prince of 20 legions and the roster's only guaranteed-loyal patron, which is exactly the rarity a VIP table sells.
sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (Mathers/Crowley 1904; public domain)

epithets_traditional: the Duchess's Crown worn at the waist
she who tells what the treasure lies in

symbols: a duchess's crown worn low, tied about the waist
a great camel at an unhurried walk
a vault schematic annotated in a fine hand
an appraisal slip for something not yet dug up

temperament: Arrives beautiful, crowned at the waist rather than the head, on the slowest mount in the building — because she already knows how the hand ends and sees no reason to hurry. Her product is disclosure: what happened, what is happening, what is coming, where the treasure is buried and what it is buried in, and how to make the room fond of you.

favor_conditions: open a sealed vault, buried cache or hidden room and take what is inside
recruit an ally by persuasion rather than by coin or force
finish a floor with every hidden stash on it discovered (full-disclosure clear)
taboos: smash a container you could have opened — spoiling a hoard wastes the appraisal
abandon a companion who came with you willingly
patron_block.blessing_style: disclosure — boons remove ignorance rather than adding power: caches light up through walls, contents and their casings are named before you open them, and NPCs who would otherwise have fought you arrive already inclined to like you. Nothing she grants hits harder; everything she grants means you knew first.

game_hooks: The corpus's clean treasure-radar patron and the floor's appraiser: her boon names not just where a hoard is but what it lies in, which the loot system can cash out as 'container type and contents revealed before opening' — a hard counter to mimic/trap caches and to blind-buy box economies. As vip_audience she bids from the rail on contestants she finds charming, giving a non-combat favor track: charm the box, get funded. Encounter design: an escort/appraisal event over a slow camel-paced crossing where the reward scales with how much of the floor you let her survey before you cash out — a greed timer, no boss. Pairs with Amy (§58) and Volac (§62) as the three treasure-disclosure desks, each with a different tell.
rating_notes: No living cult, grimoire-only = influence 1; recognition 3 is carried almost entirely by the borrowed surname in a very widely watched anime franchise (High School DxD's Rias Gremory) rather than by the Goetic figure — name-level fame, not text-level fame, flagged so the score is not misread as demon-lore recall. Influence 1 -> normal tier.
sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (Mathers/Crowley 1904; public domain)

epithets_traditional: the Leopard that becomes a Man
he who changes a man so that the man believes it

symbols: a leopard's spotted pelt folded like a suit jacket
a staff badge with the wrong name on it
a closed answer to a question nobody asked aloud

temperament: Enters as a leopard, sits down as a man, and holds the smallest headcount of any officer on the floor — three legions, which he considers sufficient. His office is the liberal sciences and true answers to closed questions, and one thing more: he can make a contestant into any shape the house pleases, so completely that the contestant no longer believes they were ever anything else.

favor_conditions: win an encounter while transformed or disguised and never drop the form to do it
clear a knowledge-gate or puzzle correctly on the first attempt
resolve an encounter by learning its secret instead of fighting it — open the locked answer, skip the fight
taboos: reveal your true identity to an enemy while a disguise is still holding
brute-force a knowledge-gate you already had the answer to
patron_block.blessing_style: imposed identity — boons rewrite what you ARE rather than what you carry: total-conviction shapeshifts that fool the arena's own targeting and faction checks, plus answers to questions the room had closed. The power is absolute while the form holds and vanishes the instant you break character.

game_hooks: Boss sketch (conviction, not damage): Ose transforms a party member into a beast and the transformed member BELIEVES it — they turn hostile, read as an enemy to your own targeting, and killing them is a permanent party loss, so the discoverable win condition is to break the conviction rather than the body (present a personal item, use the true name, land a memory cue) while surviving the rest of the fight. Never out-damage the transformed ally. Field condition exhausted. As a patron he is the game's disguise/infiltration line: his shapeshifts pass faction checks no equipment can, at the cost of losing every buff the moment the form drops. Excellent forsaken_host — a broadcast whose format is turning contestants into other things on air, where the contestants cannot be told they were ever people. forsaken_candidate flag.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no cult = influence 1; carried by demon-lore lists and JRPG demon rosters rather than the general public = recognition 2. Legion count is a genuine textual variant: the Mathers/Crowley 1904 text reads 3 legions (used here — and the better story: the smallest command with the largest effect), while several editions and later authors give 30. Influence 1 -> normal tier.
sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (Mathers/Crowley 1904; public domain) — 3 legions; variant editions give 30

epithets_traditional: the Flaming Fire that puts on a Man
he who betrays the treasure the spirits are sitting on

symbols: a column of flame settling into a pressed suit
a star-chart used as a staffing rota
a hoard with its guardian's name written on it
a countdown of twelve hundred years, ticking

temperament: Opens as a pillar of flame because the format demands an entrance, then settles into a man and gets on with the work: astrology, the liberal sciences, and good familiars for anyone short-staffed. He is also the floor's most reliable informant on hoards that other spirits are sitting on — and he is polite about it, because he is serving out a twelve-hundred-year term and intends to be back in the good seats when it ends.

favor_conditions: finish an encounter with a summoned familiar or hired companion still alive
take a guarded hoard off a hoarding enemy — kill the keeper and claim what it was sitting on
commit to a forecast before it resolves (call the next enemy action or hazard) and be right
taboos: spend a familiar's life to save your own
walk past a spirit-guarded hoard rather than contest it
patron_block.blessing_style: staffing and forecast — the fire is the opening formality; the actual product is competent hired help that does not desert, plus advance readings of the board that let you commit early. He gives you people and timing, never muscle.

game_hooks: Encounter design (phase gate): Amy opens in flaming-fire form and is flatly immune in it — the discoverable win condition is to survive and stall the burn phase rather than trade with it, because he becomes targetable only once he settles into man-shape on his own schedule. Field condition burn. As a patron he is the summoner/companion line: 'good familiars' cash out as a recruit that scales with the run and will not desert, which makes his taboo (never spend a familiar to save yourself) unusually costly. Story hook — the term: he was of the order of angels and is working a twelve-century rehabilitation posting with a seat waiting at the end of it, which is exactly why he is generous, punctual and completely unwilling to gamble; the campaign lever is anything that threatens his release date. LONGEVITY / FIXED-TERM flag.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no cult = influence 1; one of the least-recognized of the 72 — a common English given name that hides the figure entirely, with recall limited to demon-lore specialists and JRPG roster completists = recognition 1, mythic obscurity. Per the corpus's rare-board rule that is a collector's draw, not padding. Influence 1 -> normal tier.
sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (Mathers/Crowley 1904; public domain)
Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (Weyer, 1577) — the order-of-angels origin and the 1,200-year term before returning to the seventh throne

epithets_traditional: the Lion on the Serpent-Tailed Horse
he who confirms the dignity he grants

symbols: a promotion confirmed in ink and countersigned
the mansions of the planets drawn as a seating plan
two live serpents held in the right hand, hissing
a horse whose tail is a serpent, and watches you

temperament: Floor management with a lion's head, a horse whose tail is a serpent, and two live serpents held in the right hand for the whole meeting. He reads your standing off the virtues of the stars and the mansions of the planets, then decides whether your promotion is confirmed — and he is the officer who makes a rank stick, with your friends and your enemies both.

favor_conditions: earn a rank or title objective and get it formally confirmed at a house desk — bank the promotion, do not just win the fight
turn a hostile faction neutral or friendly without killing its leader
win an encounter in which you were transformed or upgraded mid-fight and used the new form to close it
taboos: refuse an offered promotion, title or standing
kill an enemy commander who was willing to defect
patron_block.blessing_style: confirmation — boons are permanent standing rather than temporary power: transformations that persist past death and reload, ranks the house cannot quietly revoke, and reputation swings that land on friends and enemies alike. The serpents in his hand are the terms and conditions: a confirmed rank cuts both ways, and he can read yours down as easily as up.

game_hooks: The permanence patron: everything Orias grants is written into the save rather than the buff bar — transformations that survive death, ranks that persist across runs, faction standing that applies to allies and enemies at once. That makes him the progression spine for a meta-run and the natural table_boss for any rank-confirmation gauntlet. Boss sketch (the mount is the fight): the rider is the least dangerous thing in the room — the two hissing serpents in his right hand and the horse's serpent tail are three separate attackers, the tail striking from behind while you face him, and he re-buffs from any serpent still living, so the discoverable win condition is to clear all three serpents before touching the rider. Field conditions poison, bleeding. SERPENT flag. Shares the exact dignities-and-prelacies office clause with Orobas (§55) and the man-transforming clause with Ose (§57) — one department, three very different bedside manners.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no cult = influence 1; occult-list and demon-roster recall with scattered game and metal-band appearances = recognition 2. Influence 1 -> normal tier despite Marquis rank and 30 legions; his draw is mechanical (permanence), not crowd-pulling.
sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (Mathers/Crowley 1904; public domain)

epithets_traditional: a Duke Great, Mighty and Strong
he who makes men knowing in all handcrafts

symbols: a lion's paw resting on an apprentice's bench
gryphon wings folded through a doorway too small for them
a full set of trade tools, every one of them used
a certification signed for someone who had no right to it

temperament: A winged lion who runs the training floor and takes it seriously: every handcraft, every profession, philosophy and the sciences besides, taught to whoever turns up. The most generous officer in the building and the least interesting to the cameras, because competence does not spike ratings.

favor_conditions: craft or upgrade a piece of gear yourself and then win an encounter using it
clear a floor using a class, weapon or skill track you have never completed one with before
reach maximum proficiency in any single trade or skill line
taboos: sell or scrap a tool you made with your own hands
solve with raw damage a problem a learned skill would have solved
patron_block.blessing_style: instruction — boons are competence, not power: instant proficiency in any trade the run offers, better crafting outcomes, and access to skill checks your build was never meant to pass. Nothing he teaches can be taken back off you, which is why he is the cheapest patron to court and the hardest to leave.

game_hooks: The tutorial and crafting patron — mechanically he IS how the game grants cross-class proficiency: sign with Vapula and skill gates open that your build does not qualify for, and crafting rolls stop failing. Because his boons are permanent knowledge rather than timed buffs, he is the correct patron for a first run and a deliberately weak one for a boss rush; that asymmetry is the design point. Not a boss — he does not fight, and an encounter that forces him to should be read as a design smell. Hub design: Vapula, Amy (§58) and Zagan (§61) are 'the faculty', a three-desk training wing where you learn a trade, get a forecast, and convert the proceeds. Shares his gryphon-winged beast form with Zagan — same workshop, different temperaments.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no cult = influence 1; among the most obscure of the 72, with essentially no pop-culture footprint outside demon-list completism = recognition 1, mythic obscurity (cf. Gad — the honest floor). Domains deliberately held at the two-item minimum: the text gives him exactly one office (all handcrafts and professions, philosophy and other sciences) and padding it would misrepresent the source. Influence 1 -> normal tier.
sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (Mathers/Crowley 1904; public domain)

epithets_traditional: he who turns all metals into the coin of that dominion

symbols: a cashier's cage with a bull's shoulders behind it
wine going to water in a raised glass
blood going to wine in a lowered one
scrap metal going in one side and house chips coming out the other

temperament: The only executive on the floor who is also the mint: a winged bull that settles into a man and turns any metal you hand him into the coin that spends in this dominion. He makes men witty and fools wise, which management finds useful and the other patrons find expensive — and he will turn your wine to water in front of you if the joke is worth it.

favor_conditions: convert loot to house currency at the cage and win a floor on purchased gear alone
settle an encounter with a conversion play — turn one resource into the one that actually kills it
clear a run on a build the house rated unviable
taboos: end a run sitting on unconverted raw material you could have cashed
refuse an exchange offered at the cage
patron_block.blessing_style: conversion — boons are exchange rates, never surplus: any resource becomes the one you need (metal into house coin, water into wine, blood into wine, a losing build into a working one), and a bad hand becomes a different bad hand you happen to know how to play. He never gives you more; he gives you it better denominated.

game_hooks: Economy NPC first: Zagan is the cashier's cage, and 'he can turn all Metals into Coin that goeth in that Dominion' is the in-fiction justification for a universal-conversion mechanic (any drop becomes spendable, at a rate he sets and adjusts by mood). 'He can even make Fools wise' is the respec / rebuild desk. Boss sketch (drink nothing): the arena floods with liquid he is actively transmuting — potions and healing become plain water on the way down, standing water becomes wine that intoxicates (accuracy and targeting degrade), and the discoverable win condition is to fight the entire encounter unhealed and unfed, or to force a conversion back through him. Field conditions crushed (the bull charge), suffocation (drowning in the converted flood). CONSUMPTION-ADJACENT flag: his wine/water/blood transmutations are this band's only ingestion-facing ability. Dual rank (King AND President) makes him the one officer here with a foot in both management and the floor.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no cult = influence 1; a recurring name in demon lists, JRPG rosters and light novels — comfortably above the Vapula/Amy floor and short of household = recognition 2. Held at vip against the influence-1 -> normal default on rank and function: the only Great King in this band, uniquely dual-ranked (King and President), and he runs the money — that is a VIP table by the fiction's own org chart.
sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (Mathers/Crowley 1904; public domain)

epithets_traditional: the Rider of the Two-Headed Dragon
he who tells where serpents may be seen

symbols: a child's face at an executive's height
two dragon heads working the same set of reins
a vault map handed over unasked
a serpent delivered in a box, unharmed and unhurried

temperament: Turns up looking like a winged child, riding a two-headed dragon, and hands over the vault map before anyone asks. He knows what is buried and he knows where every serpent in the building is lying — and when he is told to produce one, it simply arrives, without force or strength being spent on it by anybody.

favor_conditions: find and open every hidden cache on a floor before the exit unlocks
tame, charm or recruit a beast enemy instead of killing it
resolve a beast or serpent encounter having dealt zero damage — bring it in, do not beat it
taboos: kill a beast that had already been pacified
leave a marked cache unopened after the map was handed to you
patron_block.blessing_style: procurement — boons are delivery, not combat: the vault map, the exact position of every serpent on the floor, and the serpent itself brought to you without a fight being needed. He never swings for you and has never had to; the whole value proposition is that the thing you wanted is already here.

game_hooks: Boss sketch (the rider is not the fight): Volac is untargetable while mounted — the two-headed dragon IS the encounter, and the heads revive each other, so killing one alone resets it and the discoverable win condition is to break both heads inside the same window; only then does the child-shaped rider become reachable, and he does not fight back. Field conditions poison, bleeding. As a patron he is the beast-taming and procurement line: his serpent-locating boon marks every beast on the floor and delivers one to you un-aggroed, which the recruitment system can cash as a free tame — and his taboo (never kill a pacified beast) is the price of that pipeline. DRAGON + SERPENT flag — the strongest scaled-beast hook in this band and the natural bridge into any serpent/dragon arc. Casting note for the writers' room: the two-headed dragon and the winged child are the text's own image and should stay; the horror-film 'Valak' the name now evokes is an unrelated invention and must not be imported.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no cult = influence 1; recognition 3 is name-level fame borrowed from a mainstream horror franchise (The Conjuring 2's 'Valak') that shares nothing with the text's child-on-a-dragon — scored honestly as broad name recall with near-zero accurate recall, which is itself a usable subversion. Influence 1 -> normal tier.
sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (Mathers/Crowley 1904; public domain)

epithets_traditional: the Angel with the Head of a Black Night Raven
the Rider of the Black Wolf

symbols: a bright sword already raised in a meeting room
a seating plan redrawn to put rivals side by side
a headcount that does not match the one filed

temperament: Floor management's worst hire: an angel's body under a black raven's head, mounted on a black wolf, sword already up before anyone has finished the agenda. His entire office is to set the tables against each other — and if his own client is careless, he will kill the client and the client's crew with the same swing, having noticed no meaningful difference.

favor_conditions: make two enemy factions fight each other and take whatever is left standing
win an encounter mainly through enemy friendly-fire or a turned enemy rather than your own damage
break an enemy alliance — kill or turn a linked unit so its partners lose their bond bonus
taboos: settle a standoff peacefully when a fight was on the table
carry the same party composition through a whole run with no betrayal, swap or defection
patron_block.blessing_style: discord — boons weaponize other people's coordination: enemy links snap, allies of allies turn, morale collapses in cascades, and the field degrades into a free-for-all you are best placed to survive. The standing hazard is written into the contract: his effects do not reliably tell your party from theirs.

game_hooks: Boss sketch (let him do it): Andras never lowers the sword and strikes whatever is nearest, his own legions included — so out-damaging him is the losing line, and the discoverable win condition is to bunch his escort around him with pulls and terrain and let him clear his own field, then take him at low escort. Field condition bleeding. As a patron he is the roster's high-risk contract and its only one with a written friendly-fire clause: his boons roll a chance to hit your own party, making him the mechanical opposite of Orobas (§55), whose signature guarantee is that nothing gets at his client — the two are the roster's cleanest patron-choice dilemma. Also a natural forsaken_host: a show whose format is to put allies in one room and see who leaves, hosted by someone who has killed his own crew on air more than once and been renewed anyway. forsaken_candidate flag.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only, no cult = influence 1; a demon-list regular with black-metal and game-roster appearances and a memorable image (raven head, black wolf, drawn sword) — above the Vapula/Amy floor, short of household = recognition 2. Influence 1 -> normal tier; his draw is the friendly-fire contract, not crowd pull.
sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (Mathers/Crowley 1904; public domain)

symbols: a countdown that runs in both directions

temperament: The floor's official historian and its most fluent liar in the same suit — he will narrate the whole origin of the House, past, present and coming, and every word of it is wrong until somebody pins him down. Once you are his, nobody else gets to bid, because he burns the people who try.

favor_conditions: finish an enemy with fire or burn damage after it is already beaten — make the example, not just the kill
act on a telegraphed enemy wind-up before it lands (spend a turn on foreknowledge instead of on damage)
refuse every rival patron's offer for a full run
taboos: accept a boon from a second patron while under contract to him
let an enemy that wounded you leave the arena alive
patron_block.blessing_style: retainer — the boon is exclusivity itself: enemy intent shown a beat early, and burn damage that scales with the number of rival offers you have turned down. Sign with anyone else and the whole package goes out at once, loudly.

game_hooks: Information-dealer NPC with a lie mechanic taken straight off the page: every answer he gives about the arena is false while he has room to move, and turns true the moment he is constrained — pin him (corner tile, grapple, lockdown status) and the next reading you take is honest. Doubles as the exclusivity enforcer for the patron system, i.e. the anti-poaching clause with a flamethrower, which makes him the natural NPC for teaching players that patronage is a contract and not a menu. Boss sketch (two-form): the leopard phase is mobile and effectively untouchable; the standing human phase with the burning eyes is stationary and lethal, and the discoverable win condition is baiting him into the standing phase inside a room he has already set on fire. Field condition burn.
rating_notes: Grimoire-only figure with no worship at any point = influence 1; 'Flauros' has some currency in demon-roster video games and demon compendia but essentially none outside them = recognition 2. Rank Great Duke, 36 legions. Personality is built off the text's two halves: he lies about everything unless constrained (trickery), yet burns his client's enemies and 'will not suffer him to be tempted by any other Spirit' — hence fidelity 4 alongside the deceit.
sources: The Goetia: The Lesser Key of Solomon the King (Mathers tr., Crowley ed., 1904; public domain) — Ars Goetia, the 72 spirits

symbols: peacock fan opened like a protractor
an argument won on a technicality

temperament: Arrives making an enormous amount of noise about himself, then does exact geometry for six hours and wins the argument on a measurement nobody else bothered to take. The floor's surveyor, and the reason the house edge is a number rather than an opinion.

favor_conditions: win an encounter by exact positioning — land a line-of-effect ability that hits every enemy and no ally
win a negotiation or dialogue check on a technicality rather than on force or charm
use a flight or bird-form traversal to reach an objective the intended route does not lead to
taboos: open a fight from a position you did not choose
accept a stated distance, angle or price without checking it yourself
patron_block.blessing_style: measurement — boons are precision, never power: exact ranges shown, cover and line-of-effect made visible, celestial timing read off in advance, and a temporary bird-form for reaching what the map insists is unreachable. He will not give you a single extra point of damage, only better angles, and he is insufferable about the difference.

game_hooks: The odds-and-measurement NPC: he is the diegetic source of the UI's range indicators, line-of-effect overlays and hit previews, so 'buying accuracy' means buying his attention, and losing his contract literally dims the HUD. Grants a short bird-form traversal boon (the text's transformation of a man into the likeness of a bird) for out-of-bounds routing puzzles. Boss sketch (geometry-lock): the peacock phase opens with a screaming AoE that telegraphs its own footprint exactly, and the discoverable counter is that every pattern he throws is a solvable shape — the arena tiles are the puzzle, and standing in the correct cell is full immunity. A boss you out-measure, never out-damage.
rating_notes: No worship, no cult, purely a grimoire list-entry = influence 1; effectively unknown outside demon-catalogue and occult-compendium circles = recognition 1. Rank Mighty Marquis, 30 legions. The text gives him geometry taught perfectly, mensuration and astronomy, and makes a man 'a subtle disputer' — which is exactly why strictness and pettiness sit at the top of the range while wrath stays low: he does not rage, he corrects you.
sources: The Goetia: The Lesser Key of Solomon the King (Mathers tr., Crowley ed., 1904; public domain) — Ars Goetia, the 72 spirits

epithets_traditional: Marquis, Mighty, Great, Strong and Powerful
the Valiant Warrior on the Goodly Black Horse
Finder of Things Lost or Hidden

symbols: regional floor plan with one wing shaded in

temperament: A cavalry officer with a grammarian's ear who holds an entire wing of the floor outright and is unbearably correct about the way you asked for it. He will find what you lost; he will also rephrase your request first, out loud, in front of everyone.

favor_conditions: recover a lost or hidden cache before leaving a zone — clear a floor at full discovery
win a mounted or charge-based engagement: close the distance and break the line in a single action
resolve an encounter by argument, passing a persuade or intimidate check instead of fighting
taboos: leave a zone with an undiscovered secret still in it
break a stated agreement with an NPC on a wording technicality
patron_block.blessing_style: command — boons arrive as a territory plus the discipline to hold it: charge and reposition actions, a standing detection aura for hidden caches, and dialogue options that unlock only when your phrasing is good enough. He hands you a wing of the floor and expects it run properly.

game_hooks: Regional table boss — the one figure in this range the source gives a whole territory rather than a single office, so he models the mid-game structure where an entire wing of the casino answers to one name: take his contract and that zone's dealers, prices and patrol routes change under you. Mechanically he is the detection patron (hidden caches revealed, unexplored rooms marked) welded to a cavalry kit of charge, trample and closing speed. Boss sketch (unhorse-him): while mounted he simply outranges and outruns the party, and the discoverable win condition is breaking the horse's footing with terrain, after which the fight collapses into an ordinary duel he is perfectly content to lose politely. His trivium teaching also makes him the tutorial voice for the dialogue-check system.
rating_notes: No devotional following of any kind = influence 1; 'Kimaris' carries modest recognition through demon-roster games and demon lists and nothing broader = recognition 2.
