Rank Marquis, 20 legions — the smallest command in §64-72, which is why he is written as territorially proud rather than numerically strong. The source also assigns him governance over the spirits of a named world region; that is kept here strictly as the literary 'holds a territory outright' attribute feeding the table_boss role, and is deliberately not developed into real-world setting content.
sources: The Goetia: The Lesser Key of Solomon the King (Mathers tr., Crowley ed., 1904; public domain) — Ars Goetia, the 72 spirits

symbols: a trumpet with no player behind it
cue sheet with every entry marked LATE

temperament: Runs the broadcast's music and every entrance fanfare on the floor, and has never once hit a cue on time — the trumpets do arrive, magnificently, some while after you needed them. Generous with his animals, entirely unrepentant about his timing.

favor_conditions: finish an encounter with a granted familiar or companion still alive
land a finisher on the arena music's downbeat — strike inside the telegraphed rhythm window
reshape the arena to open a lane: bend or fell cover instead of walking around it
taboos: cut the arena music or mute the broadcast audio
dismiss, sell or sacrifice a familiar he granted you
patron_block.blessing_style: fanfare — enormous boons that never once arrive on the turn you ask for them. Every blessing lands a beat late, on his cue and not yours, so playing him well means playing the bar before the drop. Compensates with the best familiars on the floor, handed over without haggling.

game_hooks: The delayed-boon patron, and the cleanest mechanical translation in this range: the source says his music sounds 'but not soon or immediately', so every blessing of his resolves on a one-turn (or one-bar) delay — a very high ceiling that demands planning and is useless in a panic. He owns the arena's music stem, which lets his contracts expose boss telegraphs rhythmically rather than visually (an accessibility win as much as a mechanic). Grants companion familiars, making him the range's summon patron. Boss sketch (conductor): his attacks are scored rather than telegraphed, and the discoverable win condition is that every pattern is audible before it is visible; his terrain-bending phase then turns the arena's trees and cover into the orchestra.
rating_notes: No living veneration = influence 1; some visibility as 'the demon of music' in demon compendia and roster games, none in the general culture = recognition 2. Rank Duke Great and Strong, 29 legions; appearance unicorn-then-human. The whole patron block is built off his three stated abilities — trumpets and all manner of instruments heard but not soon, trees bent to his will, and excellent familiars given.
sources: The Goetia: The Lesser Key of Solomon the King (Mathers tr., Crowley ed., 1904; public domain) — Ars Goetia, the 72 spirits

epithets_traditional: the Two Beautiful Angels in the Chariot of Fire

symbols: org chart with the top box left blank
seniority badge worn where everyone can see it

temperament: Floor management in its purest form: he does not fight, he appoints — handing out titles, offices and standing in a beautiful voice from a burning chariot, and mentioning in passing that he outranked everyone in this building before the building existed. Not one thing he tells you survives the hour.

favor_conditions: flip a hostile faction or NPC into backing you — win over an enemy's standing without killing it
take rank over payout at a reward node: accept a title or office instead of loot
hold an appointed office to the end of a run without being stripped of it
taboos: refuse a title or promotion the house offers you
call out a house official's lie publicly, on the broadcast
patron_block.blessing_style: patronage — the boons are appointments rather than powers: rank, access, standing, a retinue that answers to your title, and NPCs who abruptly like you. Every one of them is real for exactly as long as he says it is, and he says a great many things — fidelity 1, the revocation risk of the whole range.

game_hooks: The promotions system's face: the NPC who grants titles that carry real mechanical perks — access tiers, retinue slots, price floors, dialogue gates — and who can revoke any of them silently between runs, which is the game's designed lesson that status is not a stat. His 'cause favour of friends and of foes' line is the standing-flip mechanic: spend his favour to convert a hostile faction instead of fighting it. Boss sketch (paired chariot): he fights as two beautiful angels sharing one burning chariot, and damage must be split near-evenly across both bodies or the chariot re-forms at full health; the discoverable win condition is not damage at all but defection — every legionary on that field holds a rank HE issued, so stripping or forging the appointments turns his own command against him. Field condition burn. Also a strong forsaken_host candidate: a King with nobody left to promote.
rating_notes: Influence 1 — no community venerates Belial; every appearance of the name is adversarial or symbolic. Recognition 4 — by a distance the widest reach in this range: the Hebrew Bible's beliyya'al, the Dead Sea Scrolls' War Scroll, 2 Corinthians 6:15, Milton's Paradise Lost (the famous Book II speech), plus heavy metal, games and film. DEPICTION_RISK — rated 'low' rather than 'none', and deliberately not 'living'. He carries the heaviest living-demonology overlap of §64-72: unlike his eight neighbours, who are grimoire-only list entries, Belial is a scriptural name still read aloud in living Judaism and Christianity, and modern Satanism names him among LaVey's four Crown Princes of Hell. But every one of those frames is adversary or personification, not devotion — LaVeyan Satanism is explicitly atheistic and treats the Princes as symbols, and no living community offers him worship or petition. That places him above 'none' (genuine currency inside living traditions) and below 'living', which this dataset reserves for organised modern veneration (cf. the existing Lilith record). Rank Mighty and Powerful King, 50 legions in the Mathers/Crowley 1904 text; note Weyer's earlier Pseudomonarchia gives eighty, and 50 is used here for consistency with the cited edition.
sources: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (1577) §Belial (PD) — variant legion count (eighty), not used here
The Goetia: The Lesser Key of Solomon the King (Mathers tr., Crowley ed., 1904; public domain) — Ars Goetia, the 72 spirits

epithets_traditional: Knower of the Virtues of Birds and Precious Stones

symbols: a single point of light where a person should be standing
birdcage with the door left open

temperament: The house appraiser, who can tell you what a stone is genuinely worth and what a bird is genuinely for, and who fills a room with birds that sing and drink exactly like living ones because the room looked empty to him. Downgrades your find by one grade when you are rude.

favor_conditions: identify an item's hidden properties before you equip or use it
let a summoned decoy take a hit that was aimed at you
complete a set — bring one full material or gemstone family out of a single run
taboos: sell, scrap or feed an item into a system without appraising it first
kill a non-hostile bird or beast-tagged creature in the arena
patron_block.blessing_style: appraisal — boons are knowledge of what things actually are: hidden item properties revealed, true value shown before sale, material virtues legible at a glance, and flocks of decoys convincing enough that enemy targeting genuinely cannot tell them from the party.

game_hooks: The item-identification and appraisal NPC — the natural home for the loot-grading loop (unidentified drop, his desk, revealed affixes and true value), which usefully gives the economy a face to be resented by. His similitude-birds are the range's decoy-summon mechanic: they behave like living creatures, so enemy AI cannot distinguish them from real targets. Boss sketch (find-the-real-one): he opens as an untouchable point of light and fights from behind a flock of identical birds, and the discoverable win condition comes straight out of the source — the copies all sing, but only the real one DRINKS. Watch for the bird that eats and drinks as natural birds do, hit that one, and the star drops.
rating_notes: No worship = influence 1; niche visibility through demon-roster games and demon compendia only = recognition 2. Rank Great Marquis, 30 legions. The source gives him the virtues of birds and precious stones plus bird-similitudes that fly 'singing and drinking as natural Birds do' — appraisal and decoys are both directly off the page, and the drinking detail is what turns the boss into a puzzle rather than a DPS check. His appearance is rendered here simply as a star; nothing about his figure needs any diagrammatic element to work as a character.
sources: The Goetia: The Lesser Key of Solomon the King (Mathers tr., Crowley ed., 1904; public domain) — Ars Goetia, the 72 spirits

epithets_traditional: the Beautiful Man on the Winged Horse
He That Passeth Over the Whole Earth in the Twinkling of an Eye

symbols: delivery manifest signed before it was written

temperament: Logistics: the fastest thing on the floor, crossing the whole board between one blink and the next and — uniquely in this org chart — of a genuinely pleasant nature and willing to do more or less anything asked of him. Everyone finds that deeply suspicious, which he also finds funny.

favor_conditions: complete an escort or delivery objective with the cargo undamaged
clear an encounter inside a turn-count par
return recovered stolen goods to their owner instead of keeping them
taboos: abandon a delivery or escort objective part-way
stall — end a run over par, or idle in a safe room while a timer is live
patron_block.blessing_style: expedite — boons are motion and delivery: extra actions, instant repositioning across the whole map, and rewards that arrive the moment they are earned instead of at the end of the run. The one uncomplicatedly helpful patron on the floor, with no catch anybody has yet located.

game_hooks: The courier: mechanically the movement-economy patron (teleport-to-marker, extra move actions, cargo protection) and the game's honest information broker on theft and hidden treasure — he TELLS you where the stolen thing went, and §72 Andromalius goes and gets it, which gives the two of them a ready-made two-NPC quest loop. Best used as a tonal control rod: one genuinely decent figure inside a hostile org chart makes the rest of the floor read as a choice rather than as a setting default. His sudden-abundance line, bringing things to pass on a sudden, is the burst-reward mechanic — a run where everything lands at once and early. Not a boss; if forced into one, a pure chase encounter that cannot be cornered and must instead be given a reason to stop.
rating_notes: No veneration = influence 1; essentially unknown outside demon lists = recognition 1. Rank Mighty Prince, 26 legions. The text also places him under Amaymon, King of the East, who is outside this range and not in the dataset, so that subordination is carried in the temperament rather than as a dangling relation. His personality is the deliberate outlier of §64-72: the source calls him 'of an indifferent Good Nature', and willing to do anything asked of him, which is why pettiness and wrath both sit at 1 — the only such pair in the range.
sources: The Goetia: The Lesser Key of Solomon the King (Mathers tr., Crowley ed., 1904; public domain) — Ars Goetia, the 72 spirits

epithets_traditional: the Book in the Right Hand

symbols: a book held open in the right hand
a mirror showing someone else's room

temperament: Audience analytics, seated: he knows what every single person watching is thinking, including you, and he can change it without anyone noticing the edit. Wears all their faces at once as a courtesy, so you always know which demographic you are currently talking to.

favor_conditions: swing the audience or crowd meter by a set amount inside a single encounter
resolve an encounter socially, using information the character should not have
learn an enemy's hidden motive before engaging it — scan, interrogate or read before the first blow
taboos: attack an NPC before you know what it wants
skip an offered piece of intel, readable or confession
patron_block.blessing_style: readership — boons are other people's interiors: enemy intent, hidden motives, the exact line that turns a hostile crowd warm, and remote sight of anybody anywhere on the board. He hands you the page everyone else is reading from, then keeps editing it while you look.

game_hooks: The audience-sentiment patron, which in a broadcast game show is the most powerful office in the building: grants READ INTENT (the next enemy action revealed), SWAY (convert a hostile NPC or a whole audience block), and remote viewing of any named character anywhere on the board — the source's power to show the similitude of any person 'let them be in what part of the World they Will', which is a ready-made spectator and scrying mechanic for the async global-show stage. Boss sketch (many faces): he cycles through the faces and full movesets of opponents the party has ALREADY beaten, one per phase, so the discoverable win condition is the party's own history — every counter needed has already been learned. The book in his right hand is both weak point and phase clock: it holds what everyone is thinking, and closing it ends the fight.
rating_notes: Influence 1 — no organised worship. Rated depiction_risk 'low' rather than 'none' because he draws noticeably more modern demonolatry and practitioner attention than his neighbours in this range, though nothing about that reaches the organised veneration this dataset marks 'living'. Recognition 2 — real currency in anime, manga and roster games, none with the general public. Rank Duke Great and Mighty, 36 legions; abilities as written are all arts and sciences taught, secret counsel declared, the thoughts of all men and women known AND changed at will, love caused, and any person shown by vision anywhere in the world — the most mechanically valuable ability set in §64-72 for this game specifically, since it maps one-to-one onto the audience system.
sources: The Goetia: The Lesser Key of Solomon the King (Mathers tr., Crowley ed., 1904; public domain) — Ars Goetia, the 72 spirits

epithets_traditional: the Man Holding a Great Serpent
Bringer-Back of the Thief and the Goods

temperament: Compliance and surveillance — the last name on the roster and the first one every card-counter learns. He sees every underhand dealing on the floor, he brings back both the thief and the goods, and he never lifts a hand himself: the great serpent in it does that part, and only to people who have earned it.

favor_conditions: recover a stolen item and return it to its rightful owner NPC
expose a cheating enemy or a rigged table — complete an investigation instead of a fight
finish a run with nothing in your inventory taken from a vendor, an ally or a locked container
taboos: steal from a vendor, an ally's stash or a neutral NPC
take a payoff to drop an investigation
patron_block.blessing_style: audit — boons are exposure: hidden caches and traps revealed, cheating enemies flagged on sight, stolen property tracked across zones, and damage that scales against anything the run has marked as a thief. He funds honest players and forecloses on everyone else, without ever raising his voice.

game_hooks: The compliance and anti-cheat NPC — structurally the most casino-shaped figure in the whole Goetia, and the obvious owner of the recovery loop: item stolen, thief tracked across zones, goods recovered, restitution made, punishment applied. The great serpent in his hand is a leashed-punisher mechanic — he never attacks, the serpent does, and it can only strike targets the run has flagged as thieves, so the fight is about who is flagged rather than about damage numbers. Boss sketch (clean-hands): he is fully immune to any character carrying stolen goods, and the discoverable win condition is to drop or return every stolen item before engaging — a boss that disarms itself the moment you stop cheating. Pairs directly with §70 Seere, who reports the theft that Andromalius then collects.
rating_notes: No worship at any point = influence 1; genuinely obscure even by Goetia standards, known essentially only as the seventy-second and final entry = recognition 1. Rank Earl, Great and Mighty, 36 legions. The source hands him a complete casino security brief — the thief and the goods brought back, all wickedness and underhand dealing discovered, thieves and other wicked people punished, hidden treasures found — which is why he rates a VIP table hint despite the floor-level recognition score.
sources: The Goetia: The Lesser Key of Solomon the King (Mathers tr., Crowley ed., 1904; public domain) — Ars Goetia, the 72 spirits
